parts_head.eyebrow: Four Kinds of Wind · 四種風況

parts.text_en: Below about 3 meters per second there is too little power in the wind. The rotor drifts slowly and makes nothing.
parts.text_zh: 低於每秒約 3 公尺，風裡的能量太少。轉子只會慢慢空轉，不發電。

parts.meta_en: 8 m/s · about 3 MW in the model
parts.meta_zh: 每秒 8 公尺，模型約 3 百萬瓦
parts.text_en: The blades catch the wind well, and power climbs quickly. At half this speed, there would be only one-eighth as much.
parts.text_zh: 葉片把風接得很好，功率快速上升。風速只有一半的話，功率只剩八分之一。

parts.meta_zh: 每秒 15 公尺，8 百萬瓦
parts.text_en: The generator is making all it can. The turbine twists its blades a little to spill the extra wind instead of overloading.
parts.text_zh: 發電機已經全力運轉。風機把葉片稍微轉開，把多的風放掉，免得超載。

parts.meta_zh: 每秒 33 公尺，中度颱風，停機
parts.text_en: Too dangerous to run. The blades turn edge-on to the wind, the rotor stops, and the turbine waits for the storm to pass.
parts.text_zh: 太危險，不能運轉。葉片轉到側面對著風，轉子停下來，風機等暴風過去。

lessons.parts_note_en: Meters per second times 3.6 gives kilometers per hour. Taiwan's Central Weather Administration calls a storm a typhoon once its winds reach 17.2 meters per second, a moderate typhoon at 32.7, and a strong typhoon at 51.0.
lessons.parts_note_zh: 每秒幾公尺乘以 3.6，就是每小時幾公里。中央氣象署的分級：近中心最大風速達每秒 17.2 公尺就是（輕度）颱風，32.7 是中度，51.0 以上是強烈颱風。

facts.eyebrow: Taiwan's Offshore Wind · 台灣的離岸風電
facts.zh: 就在家門口的強風海峽
facts.lead_en: The Taiwan Strait is squeezed between two mountain ranges, and in fall and winter the northeast monsoon funnels through it. That is why so many wind farms stand off Changhua.
facts.lead_zh: 台灣海峽夾在兩岸的山脈之間，秋冬的東北季風從這裡灌進來，所以彰化外海蓋了這麼多風場。

items.en: Taiwan finished its 500th offshore wind turbine on June 12, 2026, less than ten years after the first two were built in 2017.
items.zh: 2026 年 6 月 12 日完成第 500 座離岸風機，距離 2017 年第一批 2 座示範風機還不到十年。

items.en: Total offshore capacity, fifth in the world according to the Global Wind Energy Council.
items.zh: 離岸風電總裝置容量，依全球風能理事會（GWEC）排名全球第五。

items.unit_zh: 億度的十倍：100 億度以上
items.en: Offshore wind made more than 10 billion kilowatt-hours in 2025, the first year it passed that mark.
items.zh: 2025 年離岸風電發電量首度突破 100 億度。

items.unit_zh: 全球風況最好的離岸風場
items.en: A 2014 study by 4C Offshore found that 16 of the world's 20 windiest offshore sites are in the Taiwan Strait.
items.zh: 4C Offshore 2014 年的研究：全球風況最好的 20 處離岸風場，台灣海峽占 16 處。

items.en: Greater Changhua 1 and 2a: 111 turbines of 8 megawatts each, about 900 megawatts in all, 35 to 60 kilometers off the coast.
items.zh: 大彰化 1、2a 風場：111 座 8 百萬瓦風機、合計約 900 百萬瓦，離岸 35 到 60 公里。

myths.myth_en: Wind turbines need very strong winds to work.
myths.myth_zh: 風力發電機要很強的風才能發電。
myths.fact_en: Big turbines start making power at about 3 meters per second, a gentle breeze. In very strong winds they actually shut down to protect themselves.
myths.fact_zh: 大型風機在每秒約 3 公尺的微風就開始發電；風太強時反而會停機保護自己。

myths.myth_en: The blades spin fast, like a fan.
myths.myth_zh: 風機的葉片像電風扇一樣轉得很快。
myths.fact_en: A big offshore rotor turns only about ten times a minute. But because the blades are so long, their tips move at more than 300 kilometers an hour.
myths.fact_zh: 大型離岸風機的轉子每分鐘最多只轉約 10 圈；但葉片太長了，葉尖的速度超過每小時 300 公里。

myths.myth_en: A good turbine could catch all the energy in the wind.
myths.myth_zh: 好的風機可以把風的能量全部接住。
myths.fact_en: Physics sets a limit of about 59%, called the Betz limit. If a turbine took everything, the air behind it would stop and block new wind from coming in.
myths.fact_zh: 物理上限約 59%，叫做貝茲極限。要是風機把能量全拿走，後面的空氣就會停住，擋住新的風進來。

myths.myth_en: If we use the wind, someday it will run out.
myths.myth_zh: 風用久了總有一天會用完。
myths.fact_en: Wind is made by the sun heating the Earth unevenly. As long as the sun shines, the wind keeps coming back.
myths.fact_zh: 風是太陽把地球曬得不均勻產生的。只要太陽還在照，風就會一直再來。

tricks.body_en: Blades turn because of lift, the same force that holds up an airplane.
tricks.body_zh: 葉片會轉，靠的是升力，就是讓飛機浮在空中的那種力。

tricks.title_en: Twice the wind, eight times the power
tricks.body_en: Power grows with the wind speed cubed: 2 × 2 × 2 = 8.
tricks.body_zh: 功率跟風速的三次方成正比：2 × 2 × 2 ＝ 8。

tricks.title_en: Face the wind, feather in the storm
tricks.body_en: The turbine turns to face the wind, and in a storm turns its blades edge-on and stops.
tricks.body_zh: 風機會轉向迎著風；遇到暴風，就把葉片轉到側面、停下來。

tricks.body_en: The sun heats the Earth unevenly, air moves, and the turbine catches it.
tricks.body_zh: 太陽把地球曬得不均勻，空氣開始流動，風機把它接住。

materials.en: A small DC motor from a toy or science kit (it can work as a generator)
materials.zh: 一個玩具或科學教具用的小直流馬達（它也能當發電機）

materials.en: Stiff paper or a paper cup for blades, a cork or bottle cap for the hub, and tape
materials.zh: 做葉片用的厚紙或紙杯、做輪轂用的軟木塞或瓶蓋、膠帶

materials.en: A multimeter set to its smallest voltage range
materials.zh: 一台三用電表（轉到最小電壓檔）

materials.en: An electric fan
materials.zh: 一台電風扇

steps.en: Push the hub onto the motor's shaft and tape on three or four blades. Clip the motor's two wires to the meter.
steps.zh: 把輪轂套上馬達的轉軸，貼上三到四片葉片；把馬達的兩條線接到電表。

steps.en: Hold it in front of the fan on low, then medium, then high. Write down the voltage each time.
steps.zh: 放在電風扇前面，依序開弱、中、強，每次記下電壓。

steps.en: Move it closer to and farther from the fan. How fast does the reading fall as you move away?
steps.zh: 把它移近、移遠，離電扇越遠，讀數掉得多快？

steps.en: Twist the blades to different angles: flat, a little tilted, steeply tilted. Which angle works best? Real turbines change this angle to control their power.
steps.zh: 把葉片扭成不同角度：平的、稍微斜、很斜。哪個角度最好？真的風機就是靠改變這個角度來控制功率。

steps.en: Try two blades, three, and six. Why do most real turbines have three?
steps.zh: 試試兩片、三片、六片葉片。為什麼真的風機大多是三片？

activities.tip_en: Keep fingers and hair away from the fan, and use one with a safety guard. The motor makes only a small voltage, which is safe; never connect anything to a wall outlet.
activities.tip_zh: 手指和頭髮要遠離電風扇，使用有護網的電扇。小馬達發出的電壓很小，是安全的；絕不要接到牆上的插座。

materials.en: Four small paper cups, two straws, a pin, and a pencil with an eraser (to make a cup anemometer)
materials.zh: 四個小紙杯、兩根吸管、一根大頭針、一支有橡皮擦的鉛筆（做杯式風速計）

materials.en: A marker, a watch with seconds, and a ribbon
materials.zh: 一支麥克筆、有秒針的手錶、一條緞帶

steps.en: Cross the straws, tape a cup to each end with all cups facing the same way around, and pin the center to the pencil eraser so it spins freely. Mark one cup.
steps.zh: 把兩根吸管交叉，四端各貼一個紙杯（杯口朝同一個繞圈方向），中心用大頭針釘在鉛筆的橡皮擦上，讓它能自由轉動。在其中一個杯子做記號。

steps.en: Go to four places: an open field, a hallway, behind a building, and a spot near the school gate.
steps.zh: 到四個地方：空曠的操場、走廊、建築物後面、校門口附近。

steps.en: At each place, count how many times the marked cup goes around in 30 seconds. Hold up the ribbon to see which way the wind is blowing.
steps.zh: 在每個地方數 30 秒內做記號的杯子轉了幾圈，舉起緞帶看風往哪個方向吹。

steps.en: Which place would be best for a wind turbine? Compare your results with the Central Weather Administration's wind report for Changhua that day.
steps.zh: 哪裡最適合蓋風機？把結果和當天中央氣象署對彰化的風力報告比一比。

activities.tip_en: Stay on the ground. Do not climb onto roofs or walls to find wind, and come inside if there is thunder or a strong-wind warning.
activities.tip_zh: 待在地面上，不要為了找風爬上屋頂或圍牆；打雷或有強風特報時要回到室內。

safety.en: During a typhoon or strong-wind warning, stay indoors and away from the coast and windows. Wind-blown objects are dangerous.
safety.zh: 颱風或強風特報時，待在室內，遠離海邊和窗戶；被吹飛的東西很危險。

safety.en: Never climb a wind turbine tower or go near one that is being repaired.
safety.zh: 絕不攀爬風機塔架，也不要靠近正在維修的風機。

safety.en: Keep fingers, hair, and loose clothing away from fans and spinning blades, even small ones.
safety.zh: 手指、頭髮和寬鬆的衣服要遠離電風扇和轉動的葉片，小的也一樣。

safety.en: The sea near the coast can be rough in the monsoon season. Do not go into the water without an adult and a lifeguard.
safety.zh: 季風季節的近海浪很大。沒有大人和救生員，不要下水。

sources.en: How wind turbines work: lift, generators, and wind as a form of solar energy
sources.zh: 風機原理：升力、發電機、風是太陽能的一種

sources.en: Power grows with the cube of wind speed; the Betz limit is 16/27, about 59.3%
sources.zh: 功率與風速三次方成正比；貝茲極限 16/27 約 59.3%

sources.en: Windmills were used for grinding grain more than a thousand years ago
sources.zh: 風車用來磨穀物已有一千多年

sources.en: SG 8.0-167 DD: 8 MW, 167-meter rotor, 21,904 m² swept area, pitch control
sources.zh: SG 8.0-167 DD：8 MW、轉子 167 m、掃風面積 21,904 m²、變槳控制

sources.en: SG 8.0-167 DD: direct drive, about 10.3 turns a minute at most, starting at about 3 m/s, full power at about 12–13 m/s
sources.zh: SG 8.0-167 DD：直驅、最快每分鐘約 10.3 轉、約 3 m/s 切入、約 12–13 m/s 滿載

sources.en: Blades about 81.4 meters long; designed for Taiwan's typhoons and 60 Hz grid
sources.zh: 葉片長約 81.4 公尺；為台灣颱風與 60 Hz 電網設計

sources.en: Greater Changhua 1 and 2a: 111 turbines, about 900 MW, 35–60 km off Changhua
sources.zh: 大彰化 1、2a：111 座、約 900 MW、離岸 35–60 公里

sources.en: Taiwan's 500th offshore turbine (June 12, 2026), 4.8 GW, fifth in the world; over 10 billion kWh in 2025
sources.src: TechNews 科技新報（引經濟部能源署、GWEC）

sources.en: 4C Offshore: 16 of the world's 20 windiest offshore sites are in the Taiwan Strait
sources.zh: 4C Offshore：全球風況最好的 20 處離岸風場，台灣海峽占 16 處

sources.en: Typhoon strength categories: 17.2, 32.7, and 51.0 m/s
sources.zh: 颱風強度分級：每秒 17.2、32.7、51.0 公尺
sources.src: 數位時代（依中央氣象署分級）

sources.en: Taiwan High Speed Rail trains run at up to 300 km/h
sources.zh: 台灣高鐵營運最高時速 300 公里

sources.en: A standard soccer field is 105 by 68 meters (about 7,140 m²)
sources.zh: 標準足球場 105 × 68 公尺（約 7,140 平方公尺）

units.blurb_en: How a message, a phone call, and your location travel through wires, air, and space.
units.blurb_zh: 訊息、電話和你的位置，怎麼穿過電線、空氣與太空。

lessons.title: How Does the Internet Work?
lessons.blurb_en: A message to Boston is cut into numbered packets that find their own way under the ocean. Send a text or a photo in 3D, lose a packet, cut a cable, and watch the internet fix it.
lessons.blurb_zh: 傳到波士頓的訊息，會被切成有編號的封包，各自從海底找路過去。用 3D 傳文字或照片、弄丟一個封包、剪斷一條海纜，看網路怎麼自己補救。
lessons.big_idea_en: The internet cuts every message into small numbered packets. Routers pass each packet along, one hop at a time, by whatever path is open, and the receiving end puts the numbers back in order and asks for any piece that is missing.
lessons.big_idea_zh: 網際網路把每一則訊息切成一個個有編號的小封包。路由器一站一站把封包往前傳，哪條路通就走哪條；收件端再照編號排回原樣，缺了哪一片就請對方重送。

lab.title_en: A Message from Changhua to Boston
lab.title_zh: 一則從彰化到波士頓的訊息
lab.how_en: Drag to turn the map, and scroll or pinch to zoom. Press Send a text or Send a photo and follow the numbered packets. Turn on Lose a packet to see the missing piece sent again, or Cut cable A to see the routers find another way.
lab.how_zh: 拖曳可以旋轉地圖，滾輪或雙指可以縮放。按「傳文字」或「傳照片」，跟著有編號的封包走。打開「弄丟一個封包」看缺的那片怎麼重送，或打開「剪斷海纜 A」看路由器怎麼找別的路。

legend.en: Numbered cubes: packets. Each carries a piece of the message plus the address and its number.
legend.zh: 有編號的方塊：封包，各帶著訊息的一小片，加上地址和編號

legend.en: Yellow ball: a “please resend” note going back to the app's servers
legend.zh: 黃色小球：送回伺服器的「請重送」

legend.en: Dark lines under the sea: undersea fiber-optic cables
legend.zh: 海面下的深色線：海底光纖電纜

lab.scale_en: A diagram, not a real map: the shapes, distances, and number of routers are simplified, and real messaging apps may use data centers in other places. The trip is slowed down enormously. A real photo is cut into about 2,000 packets, not 10, and light in the glass of a fiber covers the 12,532 km from Changhua to Boston in a straight line in about 0.06 seconds; real routes are longer, but a message still arrives in a fraction of a second.
lab.scale_zh: 這是示意圖，不是真的地圖：形狀、距離和路由器的數量都簡化了，真實的通訊軟體也可能用別處的資料中心。旅程放慢了非常多倍。一張真的照片約切成 2,000 個封包，不是 10 個；光在光纖的玻璃裡跑完彰化到波士頓的直線距離 12,532 公里，只要約 0.06 秒，真實路線比較長，但訊息仍在一秒內就送到。
lab.credit_html: Model drawn by My Culture Connect as a teaching diagram. Cable facts from TeleGeography and the Central News Agency; packet size and the history of TCP/IP from Wikipedia. · 模型由人師教育協會自繪示意；海纜資料依 TeleGeography 與中央社，封包大小與 TCP/IP 歷史依維基百科。

paras: Your grandfather lives in Boston, and you send him a photo on LINE from Changhua. Less than a second later, his phone buzzes on the other side of the world. The photo did not fly through the air the whole way, and it did not travel in one piece. It was chopped into thousands of small pieces that raced under the Pacific Ocean and were put back together on his phone.

The internet began with a crash. On October 29, 1969, a student at UCLA tried to send the word login to a computer at a research institute about 560 kilometers away. The letters L and O arrived, and then the system crashed. So the first message on the network that grew into the internet was simply LO. In 1974, Vint Cerf and Bob Kahn described a set of rules called TCP/IP, and the network switched to those rules on January 1, 1983. The internet still runs on them today.

The big idea is packets. Your phone cuts your photo into small pieces called packets, each up to about 1,500 bytes, so a three-megabyte photo becomes about 2,000 of them. Every packet carries three things: a piece of the photo, the address where it is going, and its number in the line. Like postcards, the packets travel separately, and each one finds its own way.

Along the way, packets pass through routers, special computers that read the address and send each packet one step closer, like mail sorters at the post office. Messaging apps first send your photo to the company's computers, called servers, which pass it on to your grandfather's phone. Because each router chooses a path on its own, two packets from the same photo may take different roads and arrive out of order. If one is lost, his phone notices the missing number and asks for it again.

To cross the ocean, the packets travel through undersea cables. Almost all data that goes between continents uses these cables, not satellites. In deep water, a cable is about as thick as a garden hose, and inside are glass fibers thinner than a hair that carry the data as flashes of light. Light in glass travels about 200,000 kilometers every second, so even the 12,500 kilometers from Changhua to Boston take only a fraction of a second.

Taiwan is connected to the world by 14 international undersea cables, which come ashore at landing stations in places like Tamsui and Toucheng. Because there are many cables and many routes, the internet can keep working when one breaks. In 2023, when both cables to the Matsu Islands were cut by passing ships, the islands had very slow internet until they were repaired. That is why engineers keep building more paths: the internet works because no single road is the only road.
paras_zh: 你的爺爺住在波士頓，你在彰化用 LINE 傳一張照片給他。不到一秒，他在地球另一邊的手機就響了。這張照片並不是一路在空中飛過去的，也不是整張一起送過去的：它被切成好幾千個小片，從太平洋底下飛奔過去，再在他的手機上拼回來。
網際網路是從一次當機開始的。1969 年 10 月 29 日，加州大學洛杉磯分校的一位學生，想把 login 這個字傳到約 560 公里外一間研究機構的電腦。L 和 O 到了，系統就當機了。所以這個後來長成網際網路的網路，第一則訊息只有「LO」。1974 年，瑟夫和卡恩寫下一套叫做 TCP/IP 的規則，這個網路在 1983 年 1 月 1 日正式改用它，網際網路到今天都還在用這套規則。
最重要的觀念是「封包」。手機把你的照片切成一小片一小片，叫做封包，每個最多約 1,500 位元組，所以一張 3 MB 的照片大約會變成 2,000 個封包。每個封包都帶著三樣東西：照片的一小片、要送去的地址，以及它排在第幾號。封包就像一張張明信片，各自上路，各自找路。
一路上，封包會經過「路由器」：一種特別的電腦，會讀封包上的地址，再把它往目的地送近一步，就像郵局的分信員。通訊軟體會先把你的照片送到公司的電腦，也就是伺服器，再由伺服器轉給爺爺的手機。因為每個路由器自己決定路線，同一張照片的兩個封包可能走不同的路，到達的順序也可能亂掉。要是掉了一個，爺爺的手機會發現少了哪一號，請對方再送一次。
要越過海洋，封包走的是海底電纜。洲與洲之間的資料，幾乎全部都走海底電纜，而不是衛星。在深海裡，一條電纜大約只有水管那麼粗，裡面是比頭髮還細的玻璃光纖，用一閃一閃的光傳送資料。光在玻璃裡每秒約跑 20 萬公里，所以就算彰化到波士頓有 12,500 公里，也只要一眨眼的一小部分時間。
台灣靠 14 條國際海底電纜和世界相連，它們在淡水、頭城等地的登陸站上岸。因為電纜很多、路線很多，就算斷了一條，網路還能繼續運作。2023 年，通往馬祖的兩條海纜都被經過的船隻弄斷，馬祖的網路變得非常慢，直到修好為止。所以工程師一直在多蓋幾條路：網際網路能運作，是因為沒有哪一條路是唯一的路。
questions: What was the first message sent on the network that grew into the internet, and why was it so short?
What three things does every packet carry?
Why can the internet keep working when one undersea cable breaks?
answers: It was LO. The student was trying to type login, but the system crashed after the first two letters.
A small piece of the message, the address where it is going, and its number, so the pieces can be put back in order.
Because there are many cables and many routes. Routers send the packets another way when one path is broken.

vocab.ex: We use the internet to find information for our project.
vocab.exzh: 我們用網際網路找專題需要的資料。

vocab.ex: Each packet carries a small piece of the photo.
vocab.exzh: 每個封包都帶著照片的一小片。

vocab.ex: Restart the router if the Wi-Fi stops working.
vocab.exzh: 如果 Wi-Fi 不能用，就把路由器重新開機。

vocab.ex: Please write your address on the envelope.
vocab.exzh: 請把你的地址寫在信封上。

vocab.ex: The game is down because its server is busy.
vocab.exzh: 這個遊戲連不上，因為伺服器太忙了。

vocab.ex: A ship's anchor damaged the undersea cable.
vocab.exzh: 一艘船的錨弄壞了海底電纜。

vocab.ex: Can you connect your tablet to the classroom screen?
vocab.exzh: 你可以把平板連到教室的螢幕嗎？

vocab.ex: The bus takes a different route on Sundays.
vocab.exzh: 星期天公車走不一樣的路線。

quiz.q: What does the internet do with a photo before sending it?
options: It cuts the photo into small numbered packets
It shrinks the photo until it fits in one piece
It prints the photo and mails it
It sends the whole photo by satellite

quiz.q: What does a router do?
options: It reads a packet's address and sends it one step closer

quiz.q: Why might packets from the same photo arrive out of order?
How does most data travel between continents?
options: Through the air from tall towers

quiz.q: How many international undersea cables connected Taiwan to the world in early 2025?

parts_head.eyebrow: Try It in the Model · 在模型裡試試

parts.text_en: A real text message is so small that it fits in one packet. The model uses four so you can watch them split up.
parts.text_zh: 真正的一句話小到一個封包就裝得下；模型用四個，讓你看得到它們分頭走。

parts.meta_en: 10 in the model, about 2,000 for real
parts.meta_zh: 模型 10 個，真實約 2,000 個
parts.text_en: A three-megabyte photo becomes about 2,000 packets. Watch them arrive out of order and fall into place by number.
parts.text_zh: 一張 3 MB 的照片會變成大約 2,000 個封包。看它們到達的順序亂掉，再照編號排好。

parts.text_en: A busy router drops a packet. The receiving phone notices the gap in the numbers and asks for that one piece again.
parts.text_zh: 很忙的路由器丟掉了一個封包。收件的手機發現編號有缺，就只把那一片再要一次。

parts.text_en: With cable A cut, the routers send every packet by way of Japan. The trip is longer, but the photo still arrives.
parts.text_zh: 海纜 A 斷了，路由器把每個封包都改走經過日本的路。路比較遠，照片一樣送得到。

lessons.parts_note_en: This is what TCP/IP does for every message, web page, and video call you make, millions of times a day.
lessons.parts_note_zh: 你傳的每則訊息、看的每個網頁、打的每通視訊，TCP/IP 每天都這樣做上百萬次。

facts.eyebrow: Taiwan's Lines to the World · 台灣連到世界的線
facts.lead_en: An island's internet depends on what lies on the sea floor around it.
facts.lead_zh: 一座島的網路，靠的是它周圍海底的那些電纜。

items.en: Undersea cables linking Taiwan to the world in early 2025, with more being built.
items.zh: 2025 年初連接台灣與世界的國際海纜，還有更多正在興建。

items.en: Two in Tamsui, one in Bali, two in Toucheng, and two in Fangshan.
items.zh: 淡水 2 座、八里 1 座、頭城 2 座、枋山 2 座。

items.en: TeleGeography confirms that cables, not satellites, carry the vast majority of data between continents.
items.zh: TeleGeography 證實：洲際資料絕大多數走海纜，不是衛星。

items.en: Time for light in glass fiber to cover the 12,532 km straight line from Changhua to Boston.
items.zh: 光在玻璃光纖裡跑完彰化到波士頓 12,532 公里直線距離的時間。

items.en: The network that grew into the internet sent its first message on October 29, 1969, and crashed after two letters.
items.zh: 1969 年 10 月 29 日，網際網路的前身傳出第一則訊息，兩個字母後就當機。

myths.myth_en: The internet travels mostly through satellites in space.
myths.myth_zh: 網路大多是靠太空的衛星傳的。
myths.fact_en: Almost all data between continents travels through undersea cables. Satellites help where cables cannot reach, but they carry a small share.
myths.fact_zh: 洲與洲之間的資料幾乎全部走海底電纜。衛星用在電纜到不了的地方，但只占一小部分。

myths.myth_en: Your message travels in one piece, straight to your friend.
myths.myth_zh: 訊息是整個一起、直接送到朋友手上。
myths.fact_en: It is cut into packets that may take different routes, usually passes through the app's servers, and is put back together at the end.
myths.fact_zh: 它被切成封包、可能各走不同的路，通常還會先經過通訊軟體的伺服器，最後才拼回原樣。

myths.myth_en: Wi-Fi and the internet are the same thing.
myths.myth_zh: Wi-Fi 就是網際網路。
myths.fact_en: Wi-Fi only connects your device to the router in your home or school. From there, the data travels on cables to the rest of the internet.
myths.fact_zh: Wi-Fi 只負責把你的裝置連到家裡或學校的路由器；從那裡開始，資料走電纜到網際網路的其他地方。

myths.myth_en: If one cable breaks, the whole country goes offline.
myths.myth_zh: 一條海纜斷了，整個國家就斷網。
myths.fact_en: Routers send the traffic another way. A place with only one or two cables, like Matsu in 2023, suffers most, which is why more cables are built.
myths.fact_zh: 路由器會把資料改走別的路。只有一兩條電纜的地方受害最大，像 2023 年的馬祖，所以才要多蓋幾條。

tricks.body_en: Four steps for every message: cut it into packets, number them, send them, and rebuild them in order.
tricks.body_zh: 每則訊息四步驟：切成封包、標上編號、送出去、照順序拼回來。

tricks.body_en: They read the address and pass the packet one step closer. Nobody plans the whole trip.
tricks.body_zh: 它們讀地址，把封包往前送一步；沒有人事先規劃整趟路。

tricks.title_en: Under the sea, not in space
tricks.body_en: Between continents, the internet is mostly glass fibers lying on the ocean floor.
tricks.body_zh: 洲與洲之間的網路，大多是躺在海底的玻璃光纖。

tricks.body_en: Many cables and many routes mean one break does not stop the message.
tricks.body_zh: 電纜多、路線多，斷一條也擋不住訊息。

materials.en: A short sentence or a simple drawing cut into 8 to 12 pieces
materials.zh: 一句話或一張簡單的圖，剪成 8 到 12 片

materials.en: Envelopes or sticky notes for each piece
materials.zh: 每一片一個信封或便利貼

materials.en: Students spread around the room as routers
materials.zh: 分散站在教室各處當路由器的同學

steps.en: The sender writes on each piece: the receiver's name (the address) and a number (1 of 10, 2 of 10, and so on).
steps.zh: 寄件人在每一片寫上：收件人的名字（地址）和編號（1/10、2/10……）。

steps.en: Routers may pass a piece only to a neighbor next to them, choosing whichever neighbor seems closer to the receiver.
steps.zh: 路由器只能把紙片交給旁邊的同學，選看起來離收件人比較近的那一位。

steps.en: The teacher secretly takes one piece away (a lost packet) and later blocks one row of desks (a broken cable).
steps.zh: 老師偷偷拿走一片（掉了的封包），稍後再擋住一排桌子（斷掉的電纜）。

steps.en: The receiver lays the pieces out by number, finds the gap, and sends a request back for the missing one.
steps.zh: 收件人照編號排好，找出缺的那一號，送一張「請重送」回去。

steps.en: Talk about it: Did the pieces arrive in order? What happened when the row was blocked?
steps.zh: 討論：紙片到的順序對嗎？擋住一排之後發生了什麼事？

activities.tip_en: Time the whole relay, then remember that the real internet does the same thing for a photo of 2,000 packets in well under a second.
activities.tip_zh: 幫整場接力計時，再想想：真正的網路處理一張 2,000 個封包的照片，全程不到一秒。

materials.en: A computer or tablet with a web browser
materials.zh: 一台有瀏覽器的電腦或平板

materials.en: The free Submarine Cable Map by TeleGeography (submarinecablemap.com)
materials.zh: TeleGeography 的免費海底電纜地圖（submarinecablemap.com）

steps.en: Zoom in on Taiwan. How many cables can you count coming ashore?
steps.zh: 放大台灣。數一數有幾條電纜在台灣上岸？

steps.en: Click a cable that crosses the Pacific. Where does it land in the United States, and how long is it?
steps.zh: 點一條橫越太平洋的電纜：它在美國哪裡上岸？有多長？

steps.en: Find a cable that reaches Japan or the Philippines. Why might a cable stop at islands on the way?
steps.zh: 找一條到日本或菲律賓的電纜。為什麼電纜會在途中的島嶼停靠？

steps.en: Look at Matsu, Kinmen, and Penghu. Compare how many cables they have with Taiwan's main island.
steps.zh: 看看馬祖、金門、澎湖，比較它們和台灣本島各有幾條電纜。

activities.tip_en: Teachers can project the map for the whole class. It is a good starting point for a talk about why islands care so much about their cables.
activities.tip_zh: 老師可以把地圖投影給全班看，正好用來討論：為什麼島嶼這麼在乎自己的海纜。

safety.en: Before you send a photo, ask: would I be happy if anyone saw this? Once it leaves your phone, copies can stay on servers and other people's phones.
safety.zh: 傳照片之前先問自己：如果任何人都看得到，我會介意嗎？照片一離開手機，伺服器和別人的手機上就可能留著副本。

safety.en: Never send your address, passwords, or school name to someone you have not met in person.
safety.zh: 絕不把住址、密碼或學校名稱傳給沒有見過面的人。

safety.en: If a message or link makes you feel uncomfortable or asks for secrets, stop and show a trusted adult.
safety.zh: 收到讓你不舒服、或要你說秘密的訊息或連結，停下來，拿給信任的大人看。

safety.en: Unplug a router only with an adult's permission, and never open the case of any electronic device.
safety.zh: 要拔路由器的插頭，先問過大人；絕不打開任何電子設備的外殼。

sources.en: The first ARPANET message, “LO,” on October 29, 1969
sources.zh: 1969 年 10 月 29 日 ARPANET 第一則訊息「LO」

sources.en: TCP/IP: Cerf and Kahn's design (1974); ARPANET switched on January 1, 1983
sources.zh: TCP/IP：瑟夫與卡恩 1974 年的設計；1983 年 1 月 1 日 ARPANET 全面改用

sources.en: Ethernet packets carry up to 1,500 bytes (MTU)
sources.zh: 乙太網路封包最多 1,500 位元組（MTU）

sources.en: Submarine cables carry over 99% of data between continents
sources.zh: 洲際資料 99% 以上走海底電纜

sources.en: Light travels about 204,000 km per second in fiber
sources.zh: 光在光纖中每秒約 20.4 萬公里

sources.en: Deep-sea cables are about as thick as a garden hose
sources.zh: 深海段電纜約水管粗

sources.en: Taiwan has 14 international undersea cables and 7 landing stations
sources.zh: 台灣 14 條國際海纜、7 座登陸站

sources.en: Both cables to the Matsu Islands were cut in February 2023
sources.zh: 2023 年 2 月馬祖兩條海纜被切斷

sources.en: The free Submarine Cable Map
sources.zh: 免費的海底電纜地圖

lessons.title: How Does a Phone Call Travel Without Wires?
lessons.title_zh: 手機訊號怎麼在空中傳遞？
lessons.blurb_en: Your phone talks to a tower using invisible radio waves. Walk a hiker over a 3D mountain, watch the signal bars drop behind the ridge, then add a tower and switch to 5G.
lessons.blurb_zh: 手機用看不見的無線電波和基地台說話。在 3D 山區帶著登山客走過山脊，看訊號格數在山後掉下來，再加一座基地台、換成 5G 試試看。
lessons.big_idea_en: A phone turns your voice and data into invisible radio waves and sends them only as far as the nearest base station. The base station passes them into the cable network, so the wireless part is just the last short hop, and a mountain in the way can block it.
lessons.big_idea_zh: 手機把你的聲音和資料變成看不見的無線電波，只送到最近的基地台；基地台再把它接進電纜網路。所以無線只是最後短短的一段，而中間只要有山擋住，訊號就會被擋掉。

lab.how_en: Drag to turn the model, and scroll or pinch to zoom. Slide to walk the hiker from town over the ridge into the valley, and watch the signal bars and the line to the tower. Switch between low band and high band, add a base station in the valley, and turn the coverage map on or off.
lab.how_zh: 拖曳可以旋轉模型，滾輪或雙指可以縮放。拉動滑桿，帶著登山客從小鎮走過山脊、進到山谷，看訊號格數和連到基地台的那條線。切換低頻與高頻、在山谷加一座基地台、打開或關掉覆蓋圖。

legend.en: Ground color: the signal map. Green is full bars, yellow is weak, red is no service.
legend.zh: 地面顏色：訊號覆蓋圖。綠色滿格、黃色微弱、紅色沒有訊號

legend.en: Dashed line: the link between your phone and the base station it is using
legend.zh: 虛線：你的手機和它正在使用的基地台之間的連線

legend.en: Rings: radio waves spreading out from a base station (spacing not to scale)
legend.zh: 圓環：從基地台往外擴散的無線電波（間距不按比例）

lab.scale_en: A diagram: about 1 unit is 1 kilometer across, but the mountain and towers are drawn much taller than real. Signal strength is a teaching model, not measurements from any phone company: it weakens with distance like signals over real ground, and a mountain in the way removes more for high frequencies than for low ones. Phones turn signal strength into bars in different ways.
lab.scale_zh: 這是示意圖：水平方向約 1 單位＝1 公里，但山和基地台畫得比真的高很多。訊號強度是教學用的模型，不是任何電信業者的實測：它隨距離變弱的方式接近真實地面的情況，被山擋住時高頻損失比低頻多。各廠牌手機把訊號強度換成格數的方式也不一樣。
lab.credit_html: Model drawn by My Culture Connect as a teaching diagram. Radio facts from NASA; Taiwan's base station figures from the National Communications Commission. · 模型由人師教育協會自繪示意；無線電波依 NASA，台灣基地台數字依國家通訊傳播委員會（NCC）。

paras: You are hiking in Taiwan's mountains with your family. In the parking lot, your phone shows full bars. An hour up the trail, behind a ridge, the bars drop to one, and then to none. The phone has not changed, and neither has the network. What changed is the mountain between you and a tower you cannot see. How does a phone talk through thin air, and why can a mountain stop it?

In 1901, the Italian inventor Guglielmo Marconi sent a radio signal across the Atlantic Ocean, about 3,400 kilometers from England to Canada. The whole message was the letter S in Morse code. In 1973, Martin Cooper of Motorola made the first call from a handheld mobile phone, standing on a street in New York. His phone weighed more than a kilogram. Today's phones are far lighter, but they still use the same invisible waves.

A phone works by sending and receiving radio waves. Radio waves are a kind of light that our eyes cannot see, and they travel at the speed of light, about 300,000 kilometers every second. Your phone turns your voice into a pattern of tiny changes in a radio wave, and its antenna sends the wave out in all directions. A tower three kilometers away receives it in about ten millionths of a second.

The waves do not travel all the way to your friend. They only go as far as the nearest base station, a tower with antennas on a hill, a rooftop, or a pole. The base station connects to the cable network from Lesson 5, which carries the call the rest of the way. Each base station covers an area called a cell, which is why Americans say cell phone. As you move, your phone switches from one base station to the next without dropping the call. This switch is called a handoff.

Radio waves grow weaker as they spread out, and they lose even more strength when something solid is in the way. They can bend a little around a hilltop, but a big mountain blocks most of the signal. That is why hikers often have signal on a summit but none in the valley behind it. Lower-frequency waves travel farther and get around obstacles better. Higher-frequency waves, like the 3.5 gigahertz used for 5G, carry more data but do not reach as far, so 5G needs more base stations.

Taiwan's first 5G service began on June 30, 2020. By the end of 2025, Taiwan had more than 120,000 licensed base stations, and for the first time more of them were for 5G than for 4G. Still, nobody can put a tower behind every mountain. In an emergency, dial 112. If any phone company's base station can hear your phone, the call goes through, even without a SIM card. On long hikes, carry another way to call for help too, such as a satellite messenger.
paras_zh: 你和家人在台灣的山裡健行。在停車場時，手機訊號滿格；沿著步道走了一個小時、繞到山脊後面，格數掉到一格，然後完全沒有。手機沒變，電信網路也沒變，變的是你和一座看不見的基地台之間多了一座山。手機到底怎麼穿過空氣說話？一座山又為什麼能把它擋住？
1901 年，義大利發明家馬可尼把無線電訊號送過大西洋，從英國傳到約 3,400 公里外的加拿大，整則訊息只有摩斯電碼的一個字母 S。1973 年，摩托羅拉的庫柏站在紐約街頭，打出了第一通手持行動電話，他的電話重超過一公斤。今天的手機輕多了，但用的仍是同一種看不見的波。
手機靠著發送和接收無線電波運作。無線電波是一種眼睛看不見的光，以光速前進，每秒大約 30 萬公里。手機把你的聲音變成無線電波上一連串細微的變化，天線再把波往四面八方送出去。三公里外的基地台，大約只要十萬分之一秒就收到了。
這些波並不會一路傳到朋友那裡，它們只送到最近的基地台：裝著天線的鐵塔，可能在山頭、屋頂或電線桿上。基地台接到第五課講的電纜網路，由電纜把通話送完剩下的路。每個基地台負責一塊叫做「細胞」（cell）的區域，所以美國人把手機叫做 cell phone。你移動的時候，手機會從一個基地台換到下一個，通話不會中斷，這叫做「換手」。
無線電波越擴散越弱，碰到堅固的東西擋在中間，又會損失更多。它可以繞過山頂一點點，但一座大山會擋掉大部分的訊號。所以登山客常在山頂有訊號，到了山後的谷地卻完全沒有。頻率比較低的波傳得比較遠、也比較能繞過障礙；頻率比較高的波，像 5G 用的 3.5 GHz，能帶更多資料，但傳不了那麼遠，所以 5G 需要更多基地台。
台灣的第一個 5G 服務在 2020 年 6 月 30 日開台。到 2025 年底，台灣有超過 12 萬張基地台執照，而且 5G 的數量第一次超過了 4G。不過，沒有人能在每一座山後面都蓋基地台。遇到緊急狀況，請撥 112：只要任何一家電信業者的基地台收得到你的手機，就算沒有 SIM 卡也打得通。走長程的登山路線時，也要帶另一種求救工具，例如衛星通訊器。
questions: Where do the radio waves from your phone go first, and what happens to the call after that?
Why can you sometimes get a signal on a mountaintop but not in the valley behind it?
Why does 5G need more base stations than older networks?
answers: They go to the nearest base station. The base station passes the call into the cable network, which carries it the rest of the way.
On the mountaintop nothing blocks the path to the base station, but in the valley behind it the mountain blocks most of the radio waves.
5G uses higher-frequency waves, which carry more data but do not travel as far or get around obstacles as well, so the towers have to be closer together.

vocab.ex: My wireless earbuds connect to my phone.
vocab.exzh: 我的無線耳機連著手機。

vocab.ex: There is no phone signal in the tunnel.
vocab.exzh: 隧道裡沒有手機訊號。

vocab.ex: The radio has a long metal antenna.
vocab.exzh: 這台收音機有一根長長的金屬天線。

vocab.ex: A stone dropped in a pond makes waves in every direction.
vocab.exzh: 石頭丟進池塘，會往四面八方激起波紋。

vocab.ex: Each radio station uses its own frequency.
vocab.exzh: 每個廣播電台都有自己的頻率。

vocab.ex: The tall building blocks our view of the sea.
vocab.exzh: 那棟高樓擋住了我們看海的視線。

vocab.ex: A phone tower stands on top of the hill.
vocab.exzh: 山頂上有一座手機基地台的鐵塔。

vocab.ex: In an emergency, stay calm and call for help.
vocab.exzh: 遇到緊急情況，要保持冷靜並求救。

Radio waves cannot travel in cool air

options: Neither kind can go around anything

parts_head.eyebrow: Try It in the Model · 在模型裡試試

parts.text_en: Close to the tower with nothing in the way: full bars, and the waves arrive in a few millionths of a second.
parts.text_zh: 離基地台很近、中間沒有東西擋：滿格，電波只要幾百萬分之一秒就到。

parts.text_en: The waves bend a little over the ridge, but not enough. The phone shows no service.
parts.text_zh: 電波越過山脊只彎下來一點點，不夠。手機顯示沒有訊號。

parts.en: A new tower in the valley
parts.text_en: With a base station in the valley, the phone hands off to it and gets full bars again.
parts.text_zh: 山谷裡有了基地台，手機換手連到它，又是滿格。

parts.text_en: Higher frequency carries more data but fades faster with distance, so the green area shrinks.
parts.text_zh: 頻率高、帶的資料多，但隨距離衰減得快，所以綠色的範圍變小了。

lessons.parts_note_en: This is why phone companies build towers on hilltops, and why trails and tunnels often have dead spots.
lessons.parts_note_zh: 這就是電信業者把基地台蓋在山頭的原因，也是步道和隧道常有收不到訊號的地方的原因。

facts.eyebrow: Taiwan's Mobile Network · 台灣的行動網路
facts.lead_en: Every bar on your phone depends on a tower somewhere nearby.
facts.lead_zh: 手機上的每一格訊號，都靠附近某一座基地台。

items.en: Licensed 4G and 5G base stations in Taiwan at the end of 2025.
items.zh: 2025 年底台灣的 4G 與 5G 基地台執照數。

items.en: For the first time, 5G base stations (64,106) outnumbered 4G ones (58,905).
Chunghwa Telecom launched Taiwan's first 5G service; other companies followed within days.
items.zh: 中華電信推出台灣第一個 5G 服務，其他業者在幾天內跟進。

items.en: Radio waves travel at the speed of light, so a tower 3 km away hears your phone in about 10 millionths of a second.
items.zh: 無線電波以光速前進，3 公里外的基地台約十萬分之一秒就收到。

items.en: Works through any company's base station in range, even without a SIM card.
items.zh: 只要在任何一家業者的基地台範圍內就打得通，沒有 SIM 卡也可以。

myths.myth_en: More bars means the tower is closer.
myths.myth_zh: 格數越多，代表基地台越近。
myths.fact_en: Bars show how strong the signal is. A far tower with a clear view can beat a near tower behind a hill.
myths.fact_zh: 格數表示訊號有多強。視線沒被擋的遠方基地台，可能比躲在山後的近基地台還強。

myths.myth_en: Phones talk directly to each other.
myths.myth_zh: 手機是直接和對方的手機通話。
myths.fact_en: Each phone talks only to its nearest base station. The network of cables and towers carries the call in between.
myths.fact_zh: 每支手機只和最近的基地台說話，中間由電纜和基地台組成的網路把通話送過去。

myths.myth_en: 5G waves travel faster than 4G waves.
myths.myth_zh: 5G 的電波跑得比 4G 快。
myths.fact_en: All radio waves travel at the speed of light. 5G is faster because it carries more data at once, not because its waves move faster.
myths.fact_zh: 所有無線電波都以光速前進。5G 比較快，是因為它一次能帶更多資料，不是電波跑得比較快。

myths.myth_en: Phone signals have been shown to cause brain cancer.
myths.myth_zh: 手機訊號已被證實會造成腦癌。
myths.fact_en: A 2024 review for the World Health Organization looked at 63 studies and found no link between mobile phone use and brain cancer. Scientists keep studying the question.
myths.fact_zh: 2024 年一份為世界衛生組織做的回顧研究，分析了 63 項研究，找不到使用手機和腦癌之間的關聯；科學家仍持續研究。

tricks.body_en: Radio waves are light our eyes cannot see, and they move at the speed of light.
tricks.body_zh: 無線電波是眼睛看不見的光，以光速前進。

tricks.title_zh: 手機 → 基地台 → 電纜
tricks.body_en: The wireless part is only the first and last hop. The middle is cables.
tricks.body_zh: 無線只是頭尾兩段，中間都是電纜。

tricks.title_en: See the tower, get a signal
tricks.title_zh: 看得到基地台，就有訊號
tricks.body_en: A clear line to the tower matters more than being close to it.
tricks.body_zh: 和基地台之間沒有東西擋，比離得近更重要。

tricks.title_en: Low goes far, high carries more
tricks.title_zh: 低頻走得遠，高頻帶得多
tricks.body_en: Lower frequencies reach farther; higher frequencies carry more data over shorter distances.
tricks.body_zh: 頻率低的傳得遠；頻率高的在短距離內能帶更多資料。

activities.title_zh: 畫出收不到訊號的地方

materials.en: A teacher's or parent's phone
materials.zh: 一支老師或家長的手機

materials.en: A simple map of the school drawn on paper
materials.zh: 一張畫在紙上的簡單校園地圖

materials.en: Colored pencils: green, yellow, red
materials.zh: 綠、黃、紅三色色鉛筆

steps.en: Walk to at least eight places: classrooms, a stairwell, an elevator lobby, a basement or underground parking lot, the playground, and near the school gate.
steps.zh: 走到至少八個地方：教室、樓梯間、電梯口、地下室或地下停車場、操場、校門口附近。

steps.en: At each place, read the signal bars and color that spot on the map: green for 3–4 bars, yellow for 1–2, red for none.
steps.zh: 在每個地方看訊號格數，在地圖上塗色：3–4 格綠色、1–2 格黃色、沒有訊號紅色。

steps.en: Look at your finished map. Where are the red spots? What is between those places and the outside: thick concrete, metal, or earth?
steps.zh: 看看完成的地圖：紅色在哪裡？那些地方和外面之間隔著什麼：厚混凝土、金屬，還是泥土？

steps.en: Compare it with the coverage map in the 3D model. How is a building like a mountain?
steps.zh: 和 3D 模型的覆蓋圖比一比：一棟建築物哪裡像一座山？

activities.tip_en: An adult should hold the phone. Stay out of places that are off limits, and do not stand in the way of traffic in the parking lot.
activities.tip_zh: 手機由大人拿著。不要進入禁止進入的地方，在停車場不要站在車道上。

materials.en: Two phones (an adult's), or a phone and a landline
materials.zh: 兩支手機（大人的），或一支手機加一支市話

materials.en: Aluminum foil, plastic wrap, a paper bag, and a metal cookie tin with a lid
materials.zh: 鋁箔紙、保鮮膜、紙袋、一個有蓋的金屬餅乾盒

steps.en: Wrap one phone in plastic wrap and call it. Does it ring?
steps.zh: 用保鮮膜包住一支手機，打給它。會響嗎？

steps.en: Try the paper bag, then the closed cookie tin, then several layers of aluminum foil with no gaps.
steps.zh: 依序試紙袋、蓋上蓋子的餅乾盒、包好幾層沒有縫隙的鋁箔紙。

steps.en: Record which ones let the call through. Metal around a phone can block radio waves; this is called a Faraday cage.
steps.zh: 記錄哪些打得通。金屬把手機包起來，會擋住無線電波，這叫做「法拉第籠」。

steps.en: Talk about it: why might your phone have no signal inside an elevator?
steps.zh: 討論：為什麼在電梯裡手機常常沒訊號？

activities.tip_en: Unwrap the phone right after each test. Never put a phone, foil, or any metal in a microwave oven: it can spark and start a fire.
activities.tip_zh: 每次測完馬上把手機拿出來。絕對不要把手機、鋁箔或任何金屬放進微波爐，會冒火花甚至起火。

safety.en: Never use a phone while crossing the street or riding a bike or scooter. Look up, stop, and then use your phone.
safety.zh: 過馬路、騎腳踏車或機車時絕不使用手機。先停下來，再看手機。

safety.en: Never climb a base station tower, a pole, or a rooftop to get a better signal.
safety.zh: 絕不為了收訊爬上基地台鐵塔、電線桿或屋頂。

safety.en: Before hiking, tell someone your route, charge your phone, and keep it warm and dry. In an emergency, dial 112.
safety.zh: 登山前告訴家人路線、把手機充飽電、保持乾燥保暖。遇到緊急狀況撥 112。

safety.en: On long mountain trips, carry a satellite messenger or personal locator beacon too, because some valleys have no signal at all.
safety.zh: 長程登山要另外帶衛星通訊器或個人求救信標（PLB），因為有些山谷完全沒有訊號。

safety.en: Never put phones or metal in a microwave oven.
safety.zh: 絕不把手機或金屬放進微波爐。

lessons.title: How Does GPS Know Where You Are?
lessons.title_zh: GPS 怎麼知道你在哪裡？
lessons.blurb_en: Satellites 20,200 kilometers up keep telling the time. Turn a 3D Earth, watch circles from one, two, three, and four satellites meet at Changhua, then put the phone's clock off and see the blue dot go wrong.
lessons.blurb_zh: 兩萬公里高的衛星不停報時。轉動 3D 地球，看一、二、三、四顆衛星畫出的圓交在彰化，再讓手機的時鐘差一點點，看藍點跑掉多遠。
lessons.big_idea_en: GPS satellites keep broadcasting the exact time and where they are. Your phone measures how long each signal took to arrive, which tells it how far away each satellite is, and the place where those distances all meet is where you are.
lessons.big_idea_zh: GPS 衛星不停廣播「現在幾點、我在哪裡」。手機量出每個訊號花了多少時間才到，就知道離每顆衛星多遠；幾顆衛星的距離交會的那一點，就是你的位置。

lab.how_en: Drag to turn Earth, and scroll or pinch to zoom. Choose how many satellites your phone uses, from one to four, and watch their circles on Earth's surface. Then slide the phone's clock error and see the circles miss and the blue dot go wrong, until the fourth satellite fixes it. Turn on the close-up to look at Taiwan.
lab.how_zh: 拖曳可以旋轉地球，滾輪或雙指可以縮放。選手機要用幾顆衛星（一到四顆），看它們在地表畫出的圓；再拉動「手機時鐘誤差」，看圓交不在一點、藍點跑掉，直到第四顆衛星把它校正回來。打開「近看台灣」可以拉近看。

legend.en: Colored circles: every place on a circle is the measured distance from that satellite
legend.zh: 彩色圓：圓上每一個地方，離那顆衛星都是量到的那個距離

legend.en: Satellites: colored ones are in use, white ones are in view, gray ones are below the horizon
legend.zh: 衛星：彩色是正在用的、白色是看得到的、灰色在地平線以下

legend.en: Red pin: where you really are, in Changhua
legend.zh: 紅色圖釘：你真正的位置（彰化）

legend.en: Blue dot: where the phone calculates you are
legend.zh: 藍點：手機算出來的位置

lab.scale_en: Earth and the GPS orbits are to scale: the orbits are about 4.2 times Earth's radius from its center. The satellites are drawn far bigger than real, they move about 290 times faster, and the signals are slowed down about 20 times. The 24 satellites follow GPS's basic design of six orbits with four satellites each, but their places are not today's real positions. Earth's spin is not shown, and Earth is drawn as a perfect sphere.
lab.scale_zh: 地球與 GPS 軌道照比例：軌道離地心約 4.2 倍地球半徑。衛星畫得比真的大很多、繞得快約 290 倍，訊號則放慢約 20 倍。24 顆衛星照 GPS 的基本設計（6 個軌道、各 4 顆），但位置不是今天真實衛星的位置。地球自轉沒有畫出來，地球也畫成正圓球。
lab.credit_html: Model drawn by My Culture Connect as a teaching diagram. Coastlines from Natural Earth (public domain); orbit facts from GPS.gov. The position math is the same idea real receivers use: distances from the travel time, plus the phone's clock error as a fourth unknown. · 模型由人師教育協會自繪示意；海岸線用 Natural Earth（公有領域），軌道數字依 GPS.gov。定位的算法和真正的接收器同一個概念：用訊號時間算距離，再把手機的時鐘誤差當成第四個未知數。

paras: Open a map app, and a blue dot shows where you are, even on a quiet farm road in Changhua. Sometimes a light blue circle surrounds the dot, and the smaller the circle, the surer the app is. Walk between tall buildings, and the dot may jump to the next street. Nobody typed in your address. So how does your phone know where you are? It listens to satellites more than 20,000 kilometers above your head.

GPS stands for Global Positioning System. The United States military started the project in 1973 and launched the first satellite in 1978. At first, ordinary users got a signal that was blurred on purpose, so it was less accurate. On May 1, 2000, the United States turned the blurring off, and since then everyone gets the accurate signal for free. The system needs at least 24 satellites, and for more than ten years about 31 have been working. They fly about 20,200 kilometers up, and each one circles Earth twice a day.

Each GPS satellite carries several atomic clocks, which are extremely precise, and keeps broadcasting a simple message: which satellite it is, exactly where it is, and the exact time it sent the message. Your phone never sends anything back. It only listens. The signal is a radio wave, so it travels at the speed of light. From a satellite straight overhead, it takes about 0.07 seconds to reach you. Your phone compares the time in the message with the time the signal arrived, and travel time multiplied by the speed of light gives the distance to that satellite.

One distance is not enough. If you are 21,000 kilometers from one satellite, you could be anywhere on a huge circle on Earth's surface. A second satellite draws a second circle, and the two circles cross at only two points. A third satellite's circle passes through just one of them, and that point is you. Finding a place by measuring distances like this is called trilateration. It uses distances, not angles.

There is a catch. Light travels about 300 meters in one millionth of a second, so a tiny clock error turns into a big mistake. Your phone has a cheap quartz clock, not an atomic one. The fix is a fourth satellite. With four distances, the phone can work out its position and its own clock error at the same time. That is why GPS needs at least four satellites. Even Einstein matters here: the satellites are high up, where gravity is weaker, and they move fast, so their clocks would gain about 38 microseconds a day. Light travels about 11 kilometers in that time, so engineers set the satellite clocks to tick a tiny bit slower before launch.

Today your phone listens to more than GPS. Many phones also use Europe's Galileo, China's BeiDou, Russia's GLONASS, and Japan's QZSS, which serves the Asia-Oceania region. More satellites in view mean a better fix between tall buildings. Indoors, where satellite signals are weak, phones also use Wi-Fi and the cell towers from Lesson 6. Under open sky, a phone's GPS is usually accurate to about 5 meters. Near tall buildings, signals bounce off walls and travel farther, so the distances come out wrong and the blue dot drifts.
paras_zh: 打開地圖 App，一個藍點就標出你在哪裡，就算是在彰化安靜的田間小路上也一樣。有時候藍點外面還有一圈淺藍色的圓，圓越小，代表 App 越確定。走到高樓之間，藍點可能跳到隔壁那條街。沒有人輸入你的地址，手機到底怎麼知道你在哪裡？答案是：它在聽頭頂兩萬多公里高的衛星。
GPS 是「全球定位系統」的英文縮寫。美國軍方在 1973 年開始這個計畫，1978 年發射第一顆衛星。一開始，一般民眾收到的訊號被故意弄模糊，比較不準。2000 年 5 月 1 日，美國把這個模糊關掉，從此每個人都能免費收到準確的訊號。這個系統至少需要 24 顆衛星，十多年來大約一直有 31 顆在運作。它們飛在約 20,200 公里的高空，每顆一天繞地球兩圈。
每顆 GPS 衛星都帶著好幾個原子鐘，準得不得了，而且不停廣播一則簡單的訊息：我是哪一顆衛星、我現在的確切位置、這則訊息送出的確切時間。你的手機從來不回傳任何東西，它只負責聽。這個訊號是無線電波，以光速前進；從正上方的衛星傳下來，大約 0.07 秒到達。手機比對訊息裡的時間和訊號到達的時間，用「走了多久」乘上光速，就得到離那顆衛星多遠。
只有一段距離還不夠。如果你離一顆衛星 21,000 公里，你可能在地表上一個巨大的圓上的任何一點。第二顆衛星畫出第二個圓，兩個圓只交在兩個點。第三顆衛星的圓只通過其中一點，那一點就是你。像這樣量距離來找出位置，叫做「三邊定位」：用的是距離，不是角度。

但有個難題：光在百萬分之一秒裡就走了約 300 公尺，時鐘只要差一點點，位置就錯很多。手機裡的是便宜的石英鐘，不是原子鐘。解決辦法是第四顆衛星：有了四段距離，手機就能同時算出自己的位置和自己的時鐘誤差。這就是 GPS 至少需要四顆衛星的原因。連愛因斯坦都派上用場：衛星在高空，重力比較弱，又飛得很快，所以它們的時鐘每天會快約 38 微秒。光在這段時間能走約 11 公里，所以工程師在發射前，先把衛星的時鐘調得慢一點點。

今天的手機不只聽 GPS。很多手機也用歐洲的伽利略（Galileo）、中國的北斗、俄羅斯的格洛納斯（GLONASS），以及服務亞洲與大洋洲地區的日本準天頂衛星（QZSS）。看得到的衛星越多，在高樓之間就定得越準。在室內，衛星訊號很弱，手機還會用 Wi-Fi 和第六課講的基地台幫忙。在空曠的地方，手機的 GPS 通常準到約 5 公尺以內；在高樓旁邊，訊號會在牆上反彈、多走一段路，距離就算錯了，藍點也就跟著飄。
questions: What message does each GPS satellite keep broadcasting?
How does your phone turn a signal's travel time into a distance?
Why does GPS need at least four satellites?
answers: Which satellite it is, exactly where it is, and the exact time it sent the message.
It multiplies the travel time by the speed of light.
Three distances could find your position if the phone's clock were perfect, but phones have cheap clocks. A fourth distance lets the phone work out its own clock error too.

vocab.ex: The weather satellite sends pictures of clouds back to Earth.
vocab.exzh: 氣象衛星把雲的照片傳回地球。

vocab.ex: The Moon takes about a month to orbit Earth.
vocab.exzh: 月亮大約要一個月才繞地球一圈。

vocab.ex: The radio station broadcasts music all night.
vocab.exzh: 這個廣播電台整晚播放音樂。

vocab.ex: Please share your location so we can pick you up.
vocab.exzh: 請分享你的位置，我們好去接你。

vocab.ex: The distance from my home to school is two kilometers.
vocab.exzh: 我家到學校的距離是兩公里。

vocab.ex: We measured the classroom with a tape measure.
vocab.exzh: 我們用捲尺量了教室。

vocab.ex: Make sure your answer is accurate before you hand it in.
vocab.exzh: 交出去之前，先確定答案是準確的。

vocab.ex: The calm lake reflects the mountains like a mirror.
vocab.exzh: 平靜的湖面像鏡子一樣映出群山。

parts_head.eyebrow: Try It in the Model · 在模型裡試試

parts.text_en: One distance only tells you that you are somewhere on a huge circle on Earth's surface.
parts.text_zh: 一段距離只能告訴你：你在地表上一個巨大的圓上的某一點。

parts.text_en: Three circles cross at just one place on Earth's surface, and that place is you.
parts.text_zh: 三個圓在地表上只交在一個地方，那裡就是你。

parts.meta_zh: 每段距離多算 300 公里
parts.text_en: The three circles miss each other, and the blue dot lands hundreds of kilometers away.
parts.text_zh: 三個圓互相錯開，藍點落在幾百公里外。

parts.text_en: With one more distance, the phone works out its own clock error, and the circles meet at you again.
parts.text_zh: 多一段距離，手機就能算出自己的時鐘誤差，圓又交回你身上。

lessons.parts_note_en: Your phone does this again and again, with even more satellites, whenever you open a map.
lessons.parts_note_zh: 每次打開地圖，手機都在一次又一次做這件事，而且用的衛星比這還多。

facts.eyebrow: GPS by the Numbers · GPS 的數字
facts.lead_en: Every one of these numbers is part of putting your blue dot in the right place.
facts.lead_zh: 每一個數字，都是把藍點放對位置的一部分。

items.en: At least 24 are needed; for more than ten years, about 31 have been kept working.
items.zh: 至少需要 24 顆；十多年來一直維持約 31 顆在運作。

items.en: Each GPS satellite circles Earth twice a day.
items.zh: 每顆 GPS 衛星一天繞地球兩圈。

items.en: Time for a signal from a satellite straight overhead to reach you at the speed of light.
items.zh: 正上方衛星的訊號，以光速傳到你這裡所花的時間。

items.en: A clock off by one millionth of a second makes a distance about 300 meters wrong.
items.zh: 時鐘差百萬分之一秒，距離就差約 300 公尺。

items.en: How much faster the satellite clocks would run because of relativity if engineers did not adjust them.
items.zh: 因為相對論，衛星時鐘若不調整，每天會快這麼多。

items.en: A smartphone's GPS is typically accurate to within this distance under open sky.
items.zh: 在空曠處，手機 GPS 通常準到這個距離以內。

myths.myth_en: Your phone sends your location to the GPS satellites.
myths.myth_zh: 手機會把你的位置傳給 GPS 衛星。
myths.fact_en: GPS signals go one way. The satellites only broadcast, and your phone only listens, so the satellites never know where you are.
myths.fact_zh: GPS 訊號是單向的：衛星只負責廣播、手機只負責聽，所以衛星根本不知道你在哪裡。

myths.myth_en: GPS needs mobile data or the internet.
myths.myth_zh: GPS 要有行動數據或網路才能用。
myths.fact_en: Your phone can find its position from satellite signals alone, for free. The map pictures may need the internet, unless you download them ahead of time.
myths.fact_zh: 手機只靠衛星訊號就能定位，而且免費；需要網路的通常是地圖的圖資，事先下載離線地圖就不用。

myths.myth_en: GPS finds you by measuring angles to three satellites.
myths.myth_zh: GPS 是量三顆衛星的角度來找到你。
myths.fact_en: GPS measures distances, not angles, from the signals' travel time. And it needs at least four satellites, because the phone's clock is not perfect.
myths.fact_zh: GPS 量的是距離，不是角度，靠的是訊號走了多久；而且至少要四顆衛星，因為手機的時鐘並不完美。

myths.myth_en: The blue dot is always exactly right.
myths.myth_zh: 藍點永遠準確無誤。
myths.fact_en: Under open sky a phone is usually within about 5 meters, but buildings, bridges, and trees can block or bounce the signals. The light blue circle shows how unsure the app is.
myths.fact_zh: 在空曠處手機通常準到約 5 公尺以內，但大樓、橋和樹會擋住或反彈訊號。藍點外的淺藍色圓，就是 App 不確定的範圍。

tricks.body_en: Travel time × speed of light = how far away the satellite is.
tricks.body_zh: 訊號走的時間 × 光速 ＝ 衛星離你多遠。

tricks.title_en: One circle, two points, one place
tricks.title_zh: 一個圓、兩個點、一個位置
tricks.body_en: Each satellite adds a circle, and three circles meet at just one point.
tricks.body_zh: 每顆衛星加一個圓，三個圓只交在一點。

tricks.title_en: Three for where, one for when
tricks.title_zh: 三顆定位置，一顆對時間
tricks.body_en: The fourth satellite lets your phone fix its own clock.
tricks.body_zh: 第四顆衛星讓手機校正自己的時鐘。

tricks.body_en: Light is so fast that a tiny clock error becomes a big distance error.
tricks.body_zh: 光太快了，時鐘差一點點，距離就差很多。

safety.en: On a hike, never rely on your phone's GPS alone. Batteries run out, and the dot can drift in deep valleys. Download offline maps, carry a power bank and a paper map, and tell your family your route.
safety.zh: 登山不能只靠手機 GPS：手機會沒電，在深谷裡藍點也會飄。事先下載離線地圖、帶行動電源和紙本地圖，並把路線告訴家人。

safety.en: Do not stare at a map while you walk. Stop in a safe place, check the map, and then keep going. Never use a phone while crossing a street or riding a bike or scooter.
safety.zh: 走路時不要盯著地圖。先停在安全的地方看地圖，再繼續走。過馬路、騎腳踏車或機車時絕不用手機。

safety.en: Share your live location only with people you trust, such as your family, and turn sharing off when you no longer need it.
safety.zh: 即時位置只分享給信任的人，例如家人；不需要時就關掉分享。

safety.en: Ask a parent before you let an app use your location, and check in your phone's settings which apps can see it.
safety.zh: 讓 App 使用你的位置之前先問家長，也到手機設定裡看看有哪些 App 看得到你的位置。

safety.en: If you get lost, stop, stay calm, and call 112. Describe what you can see around you.
safety.zh: 迷路時先停下來、保持冷靜，撥 112，說出你身邊看得到的東西。

activities.title_en: Find the Hidden Town with Three Circles
activities.title_zh: 用三個圓找出藏起來的城鎮

materials.en: A printed map of Taiwan with a scale bar
materials.zh: 一張有比例尺的台灣地圖

materials.en: A drawing compass and a ruler
materials.zh: 圓規和尺

materials.en: Colored pencils
materials.zh: 色鉛筆

steps.en: The teacher secretly picks a town on the map and tells the class only its distance from three cities, such as Taichung, Tainan, and Hualien.
steps.zh: 老師偷偷在地圖上選一個城鎮，只告訴全班它離三個城市（例如台中、台南、花蓮）各多遠。

steps.en: Use the scale bar to open the compass to each distance, and draw a circle around each city in a different color.
steps.zh: 用比例尺把圓規張開到每一段距離，以每個城市為圓心，用不同顏色畫圓。

steps.en: Where do all three circles cross? That is the hidden town. With only two circles, how many possible places are there?
steps.zh: 三個圓交在哪裡？那就是藏起來的城鎮。如果只有兩個圓，有幾個可能的地方？

steps.en: Now the teacher adds the same extra distance to every number, like a clock that runs fast. Draw the circles again. Do they still meet? Shrink all three by the same amount until they do, just as the fourth satellite helps a phone do.
steps.zh: 接著老師把每段距離都多加同樣的長度，就像時鐘走快了。再畫一次：三個圓還交在一點嗎？把三個圓縮小同樣的長度，直到交在一起，這就是第四顆衛星幫手機做的事。

activities.tip_en: Compass points are sharp. Keep them on the paper, and never point them at anyone.
activities.tip_zh: 圓規的針很尖，只能放在紙上，絕對不要對著別人。

materials.en: An adult's phone with a map app
materials.zh: 一支裝有地圖 App 的大人手機

materials.en: A notebook and a pencil
materials.zh: 筆記本和鉛筆

steps.en: With an adult, open the map app in the middle of the playground and wait 30 seconds. Look at the size of the light blue circle around the dot.
steps.zh: 和大人一起，在操場正中央打開地圖 App，等 30 秒，看看藍點外淺藍色圓的大小。

steps.en: Then stand next to a tall building, under a big tree, and just inside a doorway. Each time, notice whether the light blue circle grows or the dot moves.
steps.zh: 再分別站到高樓旁、大樹下、門口內側，每次都看看淺藍色的圓有沒有變大、藍點有沒有移動。

steps.en: Make a table: the place, the circle size (small, medium, or large), and whether the dot jumped.
steps.zh: 做一張表：地點、圓的大小（小、中、大）、藍點有沒有跳。

steps.en: Talk about it: where was the dot best, and why? Think about walls and roofs that block or reflect the signals.
steps.zh: 討論：哪裡的藍點最準？為什麼？想想牆壁和屋頂怎麼擋住或反射訊號。

activities.tip_en: Stay on school grounds with an adult, and stop walking whenever you look at the screen.
activities.tip_zh: 和大人一起待在校園裡，看螢幕的時候就停下腳步。

sources.en: GPS satellites transmit one-way signals that give their position and time
sources.zh: GPS 衛星送出單向訊號，告訴你它的位置與時間

sources.en: At least 24 satellites committed, 31 flown for more than a decade, about 20,200 km up, twice a day, six orbital planes
sources.zh: 至少 24 顆、十多年來 31 顆、高約 20,200 公里、每天兩圈、六個軌道面

sources.en: Each GPS satellite contains multiple atomic clocks
sources.zh: 每顆 GPS 衛星都有好幾個原子鐘

sources.en: Smartphones typically within 4.9 m under open sky; buildings, trees, and reflections (multipath) degrade accuracy
sources.zh: 手機在空曠處通常在 4.9 公尺內；大樓、樹木與反射（多路徑）會讓它變不準

sources.en: Project began in 1973, first satellite 1978, Selective Availability turned off on May 1, 2000; four unknowns (x, y, z, and clock bias)
sources.zh: 1973 年開始、1978 年第一顆衛星、2000 年 5 月 1 日關掉「選擇可用性」；四個未知數（位置三個加時鐘誤差）

sources.en: A receiver needs distances from four or more satellites
sources.zh: 接收器需要四顆以上衛星的距離

sources.en: Relativity: satellite clocks gain 45 µs a day from weaker gravity and lose 7 µs from speed, 38 µs in all
sources.zh: 相對論：重力較弱快 45 微秒、速度造成慢 7 微秒，每天共快 38 微秒
sources.src: Richard Pogge, The Ohio State University

sources.en: The satellite clocks are set to run slightly slow before launch (10.22999999543 MHz instead of 10.23 MHz)
sources.zh: 衛星時鐘在發射前就調慢一點（10.22999999543 MHz，而不是 10.23 MHz）
sources.src: Wikipedia, “Error analysis for the Global Positioning System”

sources.en: Japan's QZSS (Michibiki) works together with GPS and serves the Asia-Oceania region
sources.zh: 日本準天頂衛星（QZSS，引路號）和 GPS 一起使用，服務亞洲與大洋洲

sources.en: Example phone using GPS, GLONASS, Galileo, QZSS, and BeiDou
sources.zh: 手機同時使用 GPS、格洛納斯、伽利略、準天頂、北斗的例子

sources.en: Phones also use Wi-Fi, mobile network towers, and sensors to find their location
sources.zh: 手機也用 Wi-Fi、行動網路基地台和感測器來定位
sources.src: Google, Android Help, “How Location Accuracy improves location”

sources.en: The blue dot and the light blue circle that shows how sure the map is
sources.zh: 藍點，以及表示地圖有多確定的淺藍色圓

lessons.title: How Does a Computer Remember Things?
lessons.blurb_en: Everything a computer remembers is stored as 0s and 1s. Type a word into a 3D memory chip, watch each letter become eight tiny cups of charge, then pull the plug and see which kind of memory forgets.
lessons.blurb_zh: 電腦記住的每一樣東西，都存成 0 和 1。在 3D 記憶體晶片裡打一個字，看每個字母變成 8 個裝電荷的小杯子；再拔掉電源，看哪一種記憶體會忘記。
lessons.big_idea_en: A computer turns words, pictures, and sounds into 0s and 1s. Each 0 or 1 is kept in a tiny cell that is either charged or empty, and billions of these cells sit in numbered rows so the computer can find them again. RAM must keep refreshing its cells and forgets when the power goes off, while flash memory locks its charge in and remembers.
lessons.big_idea_zh: 電腦把文字、圖片、聲音都變成 0 和 1。每個 0 或 1 存在一個極小的格子裡，有電荷就是 1、空的就是 0；幾十億個格子排成有編號的一排排，電腦才找得回來。RAM 要不停刷新、一斷電就忘記；快閃記憶體把電荷鎖住，關機也記得。

lab.how_en: Drag to turn the model, and scroll or pinch to zoom. Type a word and press Save to store it one row at a time, then press Read to turn the 0s and 1s back into letters. Switch between RAM and flash memory, turn the refresh off, or switch the power off and on again to see which kind of memory remembers.
lab.how_zh: 拖曳可以旋轉模型，滾輪或雙指可以縮放。輸入一個字、按「存進去」，看它一排一排存進去；再按「讀出來」，把 0 和 1 變回文字。切換 RAM 和快閃記憶體、關掉刷新，或把電源關掉再打開，看哪一種記憶體記得住。

legend.en: Full cup: a charged cell, which means 1
legend.zh: 滿的杯子：有電荷的格子，代表 1

legend.en: Empty cup: no charge, which means 0
legend.zh: 空杯子：沒有電荷，代表 0

legend.en: Yellow line: halfway. Above it, the computer reads a 1
legend.zh: 黃線：一半的位置，高過這條線就讀成 1

legend.en: Gray lid (flash memory): insulation that keeps the electrons from leaking
legend.zh: 灰色蓋子（快閃記憶體）：絕緣層，讓電子漏不出去

lab.scale_en: A diagram, hugely enlarged: a real memory chip packs billions of cells, and only 16 bytes are shown here. Real RAM is refreshed about every 64 milliseconds; here the leaking and refreshing are slowed down so you can watch them. Real cells are not cups, and real flash cells are built differently from RAM cells; the lid is only a reminder that their electrons are sealed in by insulation.
lab.scale_zh: 這是大幅放大的示意圖：真的記憶體晶片有幾十億格，這裡只畫 16 個位元組。真的 RAM 大約每 64 毫秒刷新一次，這裡把漏電和刷新放慢，讓你看得見。真的格子不是杯子，快閃記憶體的構造也和 RAM 不一樣；蓋子只是提醒你：它的電子被絕緣層封住了。
lab.credit_html: Model drawn by My Culture Connect as a teaching diagram. Memory history from the Computer History Museum; letters are stored with UTF-8, the code used by almost every webpage. · 模型由人師教育協會自繪示意；記憶體的歷史依美國電腦歷史博物館，文字用幾乎所有網頁都在用的 UTF-8 編碼存。

paras: You take a photo of the sunset over the fields in Changhua, turn off your phone, and go to sleep. The next morning, the photo is still there. But a phone is only metal, glass, and silicon. It has no brain. How can it remember a photo, a message, or your favorite song? The answer is surprisingly simple: it stores everything as 0s and 1s.

Each 0 or 1 is called a bit, which is short for binary digit. The American scientist John Tukey first used the word in 1947, and Claude Shannon made it famous in 1948. In 1970, a memory chip from Intel that held 1,024 bits began to replace older kinds of computer memory. Today a phone with 128 gigabytes of storage holds about one trillion bits. Taiwan helps make memory, too: companies such as Nanya Technology, Winbond, and Macronix produce memory chips.

How can 0s and 1s make words? Computers group bits in eights, and eight bits are called a byte. Eight bits can make 256 different patterns, enough to give every English letter its own number. The letter A is number 65, which in bits is 01000001. Most Chinese characters need three bytes, or 24 bits. Photos work the same way: each tiny dot, or pixel, usually uses 8 bits each for red, green, and blue. A 12-megapixel photo is about 288 million bits before the phone squeezes it into a smaller file.

Where are the bits kept? In a computer's working memory, called RAM, each bit sits in a microscopic cell made of a tiny switch, called a transistor, and a tiny store of electric charge, called a capacitor. A charged cell means 1, and an empty cell means 0. Billions of cells are lined up in rows, and every byte has its own number, called an address, so the computer can find any byte in an instant.

There is a problem. The charge in each cell slowly leaks away, like water from a cup with a tiny hole. So the computer refreshes its memory: it reads every cell and tops up the 1s, usually every 64 milliseconds. When you turn the power off, nothing refreshes the cells, and the 1s fade into 0s. That is why RAM forgets everything when a computer shuts down, and why work you have not saved can be lost.

So how does your phone keep your photos? It also has flash memory, invented by Fujio Masuoka at Toshiba in Japan in 1980. In flash memory, electrons are pushed into a tiny box surrounded by insulating material, so they stay there even without power. A computer uses fast RAM for the work it is doing right now and flash memory to keep your files for later. So save your work often, and keep a backup copy of the photos you love.
paras_zh: 你拍下彰化田野上的夕陽，關掉手機去睡覺。第二天早上，照片還在。可是手機只是金屬、玻璃和矽，沒有大腦，它怎麼記得住一張照片、一則訊息、你最喜歡的歌？答案簡單得令人驚訝：它把所有東西都存成 0 和 1。

每一個 0 或 1 叫做一個「位元」（bit），是 binary digit（二進位數字）的縮寫。美國科學家塔基在 1947 年最先用了這個字，夏農在 1948 年讓它出名。1970 年，英特爾一顆能存 1,024 個位元的記憶體晶片，開始取代舊式的電腦記憶體。今天一支有 128 GB 儲存空間的手機，大約存得下一兆個位元。台灣也參與製造記憶體：南亞科技、華邦電子、旺宏電子等公司都生產記憶體晶片。

0 和 1 怎麼變成文字？電腦把位元八個八個分成一組，8 個位元叫做一個「位元組」（byte）。8 個位元可以排出 256 種不同的組合，足夠讓每個英文字母都有自己的號碼。字母 A 是 65 號，寫成位元就是 01000001。大部分中文字要 3 個位元組，也就是 24 個位元。照片也是一樣：每一個小點（像素）通常用紅、綠、藍各 8 個位元。一張 1,200 萬畫素的照片，在手機把它壓縮成小檔案之前，大約有 2 億 8,800 萬個位元。
位元存在哪裡？電腦的工作記憶體叫做 RAM，每個位元住在一個極小的格子裡：一個小開關（電晶體）加上一個存電荷的小容器（電容）。有電荷代表 1，空的代表 0。幾十億個格子排成一排排，每個位元組都有自己的編號，叫做「位址」，所以電腦一瞬間就能找到任何一個位元組。
但有個問題：每個格子裡的電荷會慢慢漏掉，就像有小洞的杯子會漏水。所以電腦要「刷新」記憶體：讀過每一格，把 1 再補滿，通常每 64 毫秒一次。電源一關，就沒有人刷新，1 漸漸變成 0。這就是電腦關機後 RAM 會忘光光、還沒存檔的作業會不見的原因。
那手機怎麼留住你的照片？它還有「快閃記憶體」，是日本東芝的舛岡富士雄在 1980 年發明的。快閃記憶體把電子推進一個四周都是絕緣材料的小盒子，所以就算沒有電，電子也留在裡面。電腦用速度快的 RAM 做眼前的工作，用快閃記憶體把檔案留到以後。所以要常常存檔，你喜歡的照片也要另外備份一份。
questions: How many bits are in a byte, and how many different patterns can they make?
Why does RAM forget everything when the power goes off?
How does flash memory keep your photos when your phone is turned off?
answers: A byte has 8 bits, and they can make 256 different patterns.
The charge in each RAM cell slowly leaks away. Without power, nothing refreshes the cells, so the 1s fade into 0s.
It pushes electrons into a tiny box surrounded by insulating material, so they stay there even without power.

vocab.ex: My grandmother has a great memory for names.
vocab.exzh: 我奶奶記名字的記性很好。

vocab.ex: We store the winter clothes in a box under the bed.
vocab.exzh: 我們把冬天的衣服收在床底下的箱子裡。

vocab.ex: A phone number in Taiwan usually has ten digits.
vocab.exzh: 台灣的手機號碼通常有十位數。

vocab.ex: Each student has a code to log in to the computer.
vocab.exzh: 每個學生都有一組登入電腦的代碼。

vocab.ex: If you zoom in on a photo, you can see each pixel.
vocab.exzh: 把照片放大，就看得到一個一個像素。

vocab.ex: My phone still has half its charge.
vocab.exzh: 我的手機還有一半的電。

vocab.ex: Water leaked from the bottom of the old bucket.
vocab.exzh: 舊水桶的底部在漏水。

vocab.ex: Keep a backup of your photos in case you lose your phone.
vocab.exzh: 照片要留一份備份，以防手機不見。

options: A small piece of a chip

quiz.q: How many bits are in one byte?
Which number stands for the letter A?

options: Its cells slowly leak their charge

quiz.q: Which kind of memory keeps your photos when your phone is off?

parts_head.eyebrow: Try It in the Model · 在模型裡試試

parts.text_en: Save the letter A. Only two cups are full, the 64 and the 1, and 64 + 1 = 65.
parts.text_zh: 存一個 A：只有兩個杯子是滿的，64 和 1，64＋1＝65。

parts.text_en: Each of these two characters needs three bytes, so the word fills six rows.
parts.text_zh: 這兩個字各要 3 個位元組，所以一共占了 6 排。

parts.text_en: Watch HELLO leak away. When the power comes back, the computer reads only 0s.
parts.text_zh: 看 HELLO 慢慢漏光。電源再打開時，電腦讀到的只剩 0。

parts.text_en: The same test with flash memory: when the power comes back, HELLO is still there.
parts.text_zh: 快閃記憶體做同樣的實驗：電源再打開，HELLO 還在。

lessons.parts_note_en: Your computer uses both kinds: RAM for what it is doing right now, and flash memory or a hard drive to keep your files for later.
lessons.parts_note_zh: 電腦兩種都用：RAM 做眼前的工作，快閃記憶體或硬碟把檔案留到以後。

facts.eyebrow: Memory by the Numbers · 記憶體的數字
facts.lead_en: From one letter to a whole phone, it all comes down to counting bits.
facts.lead_zh: 從一個字母到一整支手機，說穿了都是在數位元。

items.en: Eight bits make 256 patterns, from 00000000 to 11111111.

items.unit_zh: 個位元組存一個中文字
items.en: In UTF-8, the code almost every webpage uses; an English letter needs just 1.
items.zh: 幾乎所有網頁都用的 UTF-8 編碼；英文字母只要 1 個。

items.en: This memory chip began to replace older magnetic core memory.
items.zh: 這顆記憶體晶片開始取代舊式的磁芯記憶體。

items.en: How often RAM is usually refreshed: more than 15 times every second.
items.zh: RAM 通常多久刷新一次：每秒超過 15 次。

items.unit_zh: 個位元（1,200 萬畫素照片）
items.en: 12 million pixels × 24 bits each, before the phone compresses it.
items.zh: 1,200 萬個像素 × 每個 24 位元，壓縮之前。

items.en: Roughly what a phone with 128 gigabytes of storage can hold.
items.zh: 128 GB 儲存空間的手機大約裝得下這麼多。

myths.myth_en: Turning a computer off erases everything.
myths.myth_zh: 電腦關機，所有東西都會被清掉。
myths.fact_en: Only RAM forgets. Files saved in flash memory or on a hard drive stay. That is why you save your work before you shut down.
myths.fact_zh: 只有 RAM 會忘記。存進快閃記憶體或硬碟的檔案都還在，所以關機前要先存檔。

myths.myth_en: A computer stores a picture as a tiny picture.
myths.myth_zh: 電腦把照片存成一張很小的照片。
myths.fact_en: Everything, including pictures, music, and words, is stored as numbers made of 0s and 1s.
myths.fact_zh: 所有東西，包括照片、音樂和文字，都存成由 0 和 1 組成的數字。

myths.myth_en: A Chinese character takes the same space as an English letter.
myths.myth_zh: 一個中文字和一個英文字母占的空間一樣大。
myths.fact_en: In UTF-8, most Chinese characters need three bytes, while an English letter needs only one.
myths.fact_zh: 在 UTF-8 裡，大部分中文字要 3 個位元組，英文字母只要 1 個。

myths.myth_en: When you delete a photo, it disappears right away.
myths.myth_zh: 刪掉的照片會立刻消失。
myths.fact_en: Many phones first move it to a Recently Deleted album. On an iPhone, it stays there for 30 days before it is removed for good.
myths.fact_zh: 很多手機會先把它移到「最近刪除」相簿；iPhone 會在那裡留 30 天，之後才永久刪除。

tricks.body_en: Eight 0s and 1s are enough for one English letter.
tricks.body_zh: 8 個 0 和 1，就夠存一個英文字母。

tricks.body_en: A charged cell is a 1; an empty cell is a 0.
tricks.body_zh: 有電荷的格子是 1，空的格子是 0。

tricks.body_en: RAM needs power and refreshing; flash keeps its charge locked in.
tricks.body_zh: RAM 要有電、要刷新；快閃記憶體把電荷鎖住。

tricks.body_en: Work in RAM is lost when the power goes off, so save it and back it up.
tricks.body_zh: RAM 裡的東西一斷電就沒了，所以要存檔、要備份。

safety.en: Never take apart a phone, tablet, or laptop to look at its chips. The lithium battery inside can catch fire if it is bent or punctured.
safety.zh: 絕不要拆開手機、平板或筆電看裡面的晶片：裡面的鋰電池被折到或刺破，可能會起火。

safety.en: Save your work often, and with a parent's help, back up important photos and files in a second place.
safety.zh: 作業要常常存檔；重要的照片和檔案，請家長幫忙另外備份一份。

safety.en: Never share your passwords, even with friends.
safety.zh: 密碼絕不告訴別人，就算是好朋友也一樣。

safety.en: Do not plug in a USB drive that you found or that came from a stranger. It could carry harmful software.
safety.zh: 撿到的或陌生人給的隨身碟不要插，裡面可能有惡意程式。

safety.en: Before an old phone is given away or recycled, ask an adult to back it up and reset it, so your photos and messages are erased.
safety.zh: 舊手機送人或回收之前，請大人先備份、再重設，把你的照片和訊息清掉。

activities.title_zh: 用 0 和 1 寫你的名字

materials.en: A table of capital letters and their numbers: A = 65, B = 66, and so on to Z = 90
materials.zh: 一張大寫字母號碼表：A＝65、B＝66……一直到 Z＝90

materials.en: Eight cards labeled 128, 64, 32, 16, 8, 4, 2, 1
Grid paper and two colors of pencils
materials.zh: 方格紙和兩種顏色的色鉛筆

steps.en: Find the number for each letter of your English name in capital letters.
steps.zh: 用大寫字母，找出你英文名字每個字母的號碼。

steps.en: Make each number by adding cards, starting from 128. Write 1 under each card you use and 0 under each card you skip. For example, A = 64 + 1 = 01000001.
steps.zh: 從 128 開始用卡片湊出每個號碼：用到的卡片寫 1、沒用到的寫 0。例如 A＝64＋1＝01000001。

steps.en: Color eight squares for each letter: dark for 1, light for 0. Your name is now a strip of bytes.
steps.zh: 每個字母塗 8 格：1 塗深色、0 塗淺色。你的名字就變成一條位元組。

steps.en: Trade strips with a partner and decode each other's names.
steps.zh: 和同學交換紙條，解出對方的名字。

activities.tip_en: Check your work: every capital letter starts with 010.
activities.tip_zh: 檢查一下：每個大寫字母都是 010 開頭。

activities.title_zh: 用 0 和 1 畫一張圖

materials.en: Grid paper with 8 × 8 squares
materials.zh: 8 × 8 格的方格紙

materials.en: A pencil and an eraser
materials.zh: 鉛筆和橡皮擦

steps.en: The teacher reads eight rows of eight 0s and 1s. Fill in each square that is a 1.
steps.zh: 老師唸出 8 排、每排 8 個 0 和 1，是 1 的格子就塗黑。

steps.en: Look at the finished grid. What picture appears?
steps.zh: 看看完成的方格，出現了什麼圖案？

steps.en: Draw your own 8 × 8 picture, write each row as eight bits, and read it to a partner to copy.
steps.zh: 自己畫一張 8 × 8 的圖，把每一排寫成 8 個位元，唸給同學聽，讓他畫出來。

steps.en: Talk about it: your picture used 64 bits. A 12-megapixel phone photo uses 12 million pixels with 24 bits each. How many bits is that?
steps.zh: 討論：你的圖用了 64 個位元。一張 1,200 萬畫素的手機照片有 1,200 萬個像素、每個 24 位元，總共幾個位元？

activities.tip_en: Use a pencil so you can fix mistakes, and read each row slowly.
activities.tip_zh: 用鉛筆，畫錯可以擦；每一排要唸慢一點。

sources.en: Tukey shortened “binary digit” to “bit” in a 1947 Bell Labs memo; Shannon introduced it in 1948
sources.zh: 塔基 1947 年在貝爾實驗室備忘錄把 binary digit 縮成 bit；夏農 1948 年正式使用

sources.en: Intel's 1103 (1970), a 1,024-bit DRAM, began to replace magnetic core memory; Dennard's single-transistor cell
sources.zh: 英特爾 1103（1970）1,024 位元 DRAM 開始取代磁芯記憶體；丹納德的單電晶體格子

sources.en: A DRAM cell is a capacitor and a transistor; refreshed often every 64 ms
sources.zh: DRAM 格子是一個電容加一個電晶體；通常每 64 毫秒刷新

sources.en: Flash memory invented by Fujio Masuoka at Toshiba in 1980; charge kept in an insulated gate
sources.zh: 快閃記憶體由東芝的舛岡富士雄在 1980 年發明；電荷存在被絕緣層包住的閘極

sources.en: ASCII: 128 codes for English letters, digits, and symbols
sources.zh: ASCII：128 個代碼，給英文字母、數字與符號

sources.en: UTF-8: one to four bytes per character; most Chinese characters need three; used by almost every webpage
sources.zh: UTF-8：每個字 1 到 4 個位元組，大部分中文字 3 個；幾乎所有網頁都用

sources.en: 24-bit color: 8 bits each for red, green, and blue
sources.zh: 24 位元色彩：紅綠藍各 8 位元

sources.en: Nanya Technology makes DRAM
sources.zh: 南亞科技生產 DRAM

sources.en: Winbond (headquartered in Taichung) makes DRAM and flash memory
sources.zh: 華邦電子（總部台中）生產 DRAM 與快閃記憶體

sources.en: Macronix, headquartered in Taiwan, makes flash memory
sources.zh: 旺宏電子（總部在台灣）生產快閃記憶體

sources.en: Deleted photos stay in Recently Deleted for 30 days on iPhone
sources.zh: iPhone 刪除的照片會在「最近刪除」留 30 天

units.blurb_en: Why the sky is blue, where rainbows come from, and how sounds and pictures are captured.
units.blurb_zh: 天空為什麼是藍的、彩虹從哪裡來，聲音和影像怎麼被捕捉下來。

lessons.title: Why Is the Sky Blue?
lessons.blurb_en: Sunlight looks white, so why is the sky blue and the sunset red? Watch light cross the air in 3D, slide the Sun down to the horizon, and see the sky change color over Changhua.
lessons.blurb_zh: 陽光看起來是白的，天空為什麼是藍的、夕陽又為什麼是紅的？在 3D 裡看光穿過大氣，把太陽拉到地平線，看彰化的天空怎麼變色。
lessons.big_idea_en: Sunlight is every color mixed together. Air molecules are much smaller than light waves, and they scatter short blue waves several times more than long red ones, so blue light reaches your eyes from every part of the sky. At sunset, sunlight crosses far more air, the blue is scattered away on the way, and the light that is left is orange and red.
lessons.big_idea_zh: 陽光是各種顏色混在一起的光。空氣分子比光的波長小很多，把波長短的藍光散射得比波長長的紅光多好幾倍，所以天空的每個方向都有藍光射進你的眼睛。日落時陽光要穿過多得多的空氣，藍光在半路就被散射掉，剩下的就是橙色和紅色。

lab.how_en: Drag to turn the model, and scroll or pinch to zoom. Slide the Sun from high in the sky down to the horizon and watch the colored light particles: blue ones bounce off in every direction, while red ones mostly keep going straight. The small window shows the sky and the Sun as you would see them from Changhua. Turn off the air to see a sky like the Moon's.
lab.how_zh: 拖曳可以旋轉模型，滾輪或雙指可以縮放。把太陽從高空拉到地平線，看彩色的光子：藍色的往四面八方彈開，紅色的大多直直往前走。右邊的小窗是你在彰化會看到的天空和太陽。關掉「大氣」，看看像月球那樣的天空。

legend.en: Blue dots: blue light, which the air scatters several times more than red
legend.zh: 藍點：藍光，空氣散射它比紅光多好幾倍

legend.en: Red dots: red light, which mostly passes straight through
legend.zh: 紅點：紅光，大多直直穿過去

legend.en: Dashed line: the sunlight's path through the air to you
legend.zh: 虛線：陽光穿過大氣到你這裡的路

legend.en: Blue shell: the air, drawn much thicker than real
legend.zh: 藍色外殼：大氣，畫得比真的厚很多

lab.scale_en: A diagram: compared with Earth, the air is drawn many times thicker than it really is, and the light particles move slowly so you can follow them. Only five colors are shown. The numbers and the colors in the small window are calculated for clean air, counting each bounce once; real skies also have dust, smoke, and clouds, which can make sunsets redder or duller.
lab.scale_zh: 這是示意圖：和地球相比，大氣畫得比真的厚很多倍，光子也走得很慢，讓你跟得上。只畫了五種顏色。小窗裡的數字和顏色是用乾淨空氣、每道光只彈一次算出來的；真正的天空還有灰塵、煙和雲，夕陽可能更紅，也可能更暗淡。
lab.credit_html: Model drawn by My Culture Connect as a teaching diagram. Scattering facts from NASA Space Place and the UC Riverside Physics FAQ; the amount of air at each Sun height uses the Kasten and Young (1989) formula. · 模型由人師教育協會自繪示意；散射依 NASA Space Place 與加州大學河濱分校物理 FAQ，太陽在各高度穿過的空氣量用 Kasten 與 Young（1989）的公式。

paras: Look up on a clear day in Changhua, and the sky is bright blue. Wait until evening, stand on the coast facing the Taiwan Strait, and the setting Sun glows orange and red. But sunlight looks white, and the air looks clear. So where does the blue come from, and why does the Sun change color at the end of the day?

In 1672, Isaac Newton reported that a glass prism splits white sunlight into a rainbow of colors. White light is really every color mixed together. Each color is a light wave with its own length: red waves are the longest we can see, and blue and violet waves are the shortest. In 1859, John Tyndall showed that tiny particles scatter blue light more than red, and in 1871, Lord Rayleigh worked out the exact rule.

Here is Rayleigh's rule. Air molecules are far smaller than light waves. When sunlight hits them, they scatter a little of it in every direction, and the shorter the wave, the more it is scattered. Blue light is scattered several times more than red light. As sunlight crosses the air, blue light bounces off in all directions, so wherever you look in the sky, blue light is coming toward your eyes.

Violet waves are even shorter, so why isn't the sky violet? Sunlight has less violet than blue to begin with, some violet is absorbed high in the air, and our eyes are less sensitive to violet. The mix that reaches us looks sky blue. Clouds are different. Their water droplets are much bigger than light waves, so they scatter all colors about equally, and clouds look white or gray.

At sunset, sunlight arrives almost sideways. Instead of crossing the air straight down, it travels through up to about 38 times as much air. Along that long path, almost all the blue is scattered away, and mostly orange and red light reaches you. Dust and smoke can make sunsets even redder. This reddened light even reaches the Moon during a total lunar eclipse and turns it a coppery red, as you learned in the astronomy series.

Without air, there would be no blue sky. On the Moon, which has almost no air, the sky is black even in the daytime. On Mars, the thin air is full of fine dust, so the daytime sky looks orange or reddish, and the sky around the setting Sun turns blue-gray, the opposite of Earth. Next time you see a blue sky or a red sunset, remember that you are seeing sunlight bounce off the air above you.
paras_zh: 晴天在彰化抬頭看，天空是亮亮的藍色。等到傍晚，站在面向台灣海峽的海邊，落日發出橙紅的光。可是陽光看起來是白的，空氣看起來是透明的。藍色到底從哪裡來？太陽在一天結束時又為什麼變了顏色？
1672 年，牛頓發表：一塊玻璃稜鏡能把白色的陽光分成彩虹般的顏色。白光其實是所有顏色混在一起。每種顏色都是一種光波，有自己的波長：紅光是我們看得到的光裡波長最長的，藍光和紫光最短。1859 年，丁達爾發現細小的微粒散射藍光比紅光多；1871 年，瑞利找出了確切的規則。
瑞利的規則是這樣的：空氣分子比光的波長小很多很多。陽光碰到它們，就有一點點被散射到四面八方，而且波越短，被散射得越多。藍光被散射的量是紅光的好幾倍。陽光穿過空氣時，藍光往四處彈開，所以不管你看向天空的哪裡，都有藍光朝你的眼睛射過來。
紫光的波更短，天空為什麼不是紫色的？因為陽光裡的紫光本來就比藍光少，有些紫光在高空就被吸收了，我們的眼睛對紫光也比較不敏感。最後進到眼睛的混合光，看起來就是天藍色。雲就不一樣了：雲裡的小水滴比光的波長大很多，各種顏色都散射得差不多，所以雲看起來是白色或灰色。
日落時，陽光幾乎是橫著照過來的。它不是垂直穿過空氣，而是要穿過最多約 38 倍的空氣。在這麼長的路上，藍光幾乎全被散射掉，到達你眼前的大多是橙光和紅光。灰塵和煙會讓夕陽更紅。這些變紅的光甚至會照到月亮上：月全食時月亮變成古銅紅色，就是天文系列講過的那件事。
沒有空氣，就沒有藍天。月球幾乎沒有空氣，就算是白天，天空也是黑的。火星的空氣很稀薄、又充滿細細的灰塵，所以白天的天空是橙色或偏紅，落日旁邊的天空反而變成藍灰色，正好和地球相反。下次看到藍天或紅色的夕陽，記得：你看到的是陽光在你頭頂的空氣裡彈來彈去。
questions: Why does the air scatter blue light more than red light?
If violet light is scattered even more, why isn't the sky violet?
Why does the Sun look orange or red at sunset?
answers: Air molecules are much smaller than light waves, and the shorter the wave, the more it is scattered. Blue waves are shorter than red waves.
Sunlight has less violet than blue, some violet is absorbed high in the air, and our eyes are less sensitive to violet.
At sunset, sunlight crosses up to about 38 times as much air, so almost all the blue is scattered away before it reaches you, leaving mostly orange and red.

vocab.exzh: 風把葉子吹得滿院子都是。
