Take the elevator because it is faster

parts_head.eyebrow: Try It in the Model · 在模型裡試試

parts.text_en: With six riders the car weighs 1,420 kg and the counterweight 1,450 kg. The motor holds only 30 kg: almost a perfect balance.
parts.text_zh: 6 位乘客時，車廂重 1,420 公斤，平衡錘 1,450 公斤。馬達只要撐住 30 公斤，幾乎完全平衡。

parts.text_en: A full car weighs 1,840 kg, but the motor holds only the 390 kg difference. The counterweight carries the rest.
parts.text_zh: 坐滿的車廂重 1,840 公斤，但馬達只撐住相差的 390 公斤，其他的都由平衡錘分擔。

parts.text_en: Take the counterweight away and the motor must hold all 1,840 kg by itself, nearly five times as much. In the model, the motor glows orange.
parts.text_zh: 把平衡錘拿掉，馬達就得自己撐住全部的 1,840 公斤，將近五倍。模型裡的馬達會發出橘光。

parts.text_en: Every cable is cut at once. The car begins to fall, the governor feels the speed, and the red safety brakes grip the rails.
parts.text_zh: 所有的鋼索同時被剪斷。車廂開始往下掉，調速機察覺速度不對，紅色的安全裝置就夾住導軌。

lessons.parts_note_en: Watch the two bars in the panel: the green one is what the motor holds with a counterweight, and the red one is what it would hold without it.
lessons.parts_note_zh: 注意面板上的兩條橫槓：綠色是有平衡錘時馬達要撐住的重量，紅色是沒有平衡錘時要撐住的重量。

facts.eyebrow: Elevators by the Numbers · 電梯的數字
facts.en: From a cut rope to Taipei 101
facts.lead_en: Safe elevators are the reason cities could grow tall.
facts.lead_zh: 有了安全的電梯，城市才蓋得出高樓。

items.en: Elisha Otis invented a device that stops an elevator if its rope breaks, and showed it in New York in 1854.
items.zh: 奧的斯發明了繩子斷掉時能把電梯停住的裝置，1854 年在紐約公開示範。

items.unit_zh: 第一部載客的安全電梯
items.en: It opened on March 23, 1857, in a five-story store on Broadway in New York City.
items.zh: 1857 年 3 月 23 日，在紐約百老匯街一棟五層樓的商店裡啟用。

items.en: A counterweight usually weighs as much as the car plus 40 to 50 percent of the load it can carry.
items.zh: 平衡錘的重量，通常等於車廂加上可載重量的 40% 到 50%。

items.en: A car usually hangs on 2 to 6 cables. Each one alone can hold a full car, plus 25 percent more.
items.zh: 車廂通常掛在 2 到 6 條鋼索上，每一條都能單獨吊住滿載的車廂，還多出 25%。

items.en: The time Taipei 101's elevators take from the 5th floor to the observatory on the 89th.
items.zh: 台北 101 的電梯從 5 樓到 89 樓觀景台所需的時間。

items.en: The top speed of Taipei 101's elevators going up, the fastest in the world when the tower opened.
items.zh: 台北 101 電梯上升的最高速度，啟用時是全世界最快。

myths.myth_en: The motor lifts the whole weight of the car and everyone in it.
myths.myth_zh: 馬達把整個車廂和裡面所有的人硬舉起來。
myths.fact_en: The counterweight balances most of that weight. The motor only moves the difference between the two sides.
myths.fact_zh: 大部分的重量由平衡錘抵消，馬達只搬動兩邊的重量差。

myths.myth_en: If a cable breaks, the elevator falls all the way to the bottom.
myths.myth_zh: 鋼索一斷，電梯就會一路摔到底。
myths.fact_en: A car hangs on several cables, and each one alone can hold it. If it still moves down too fast, safety brakes grip the rails.
myths.fact_zh: 車廂掛在好幾條鋼索上，每一條都能單獨吊住它。就算真的往下跑太快，安全裝置也會夾住導軌。

myths.myth_en: A heavier counterweight is always better.
myths.myth_zh: 平衡錘越重越好。
myths.fact_en: Too heavy is as bad as too light. It is sized to balance a car that is about half full, the middle of what the elevator carries.
myths.fact_zh: 太重和太輕一樣不好。它的重量剛好平衡「大約半滿」的車廂，也就是電梯載重的中間值。

myths.myth_en: In a fire, the elevator is the fastest way out.
myths.myth_zh: 火災時搭電梯逃生最快。
myths.fact_en: Never use an elevator in a fire. The power may go out and trap you inside. Take the stairs.
myths.fact_zh: 火災時絕對不可以搭電梯，可能停電把你困在裡面。請走樓梯。

tricks.body_en: Car on one side, counterweight on the other. One goes up, the other comes down.
tricks.body_zh: 一邊是車廂，一邊是平衡錘。一個上去，另一個就下來。

tricks.body_en: The motor does not lift the car. It moves the difference between the two sides.
tricks.body_zh: 馬達不是舉起車廂，是搬動兩邊的重量差。

tricks.body_en: The counterweight matches a half-full car, so that is when the motor works least.
tricks.body_zh: 平衡錘和半滿的車廂一樣重，所以那時候馬達最省力。

tricks.body_en: A governor watches the speed. Too fast going down, and the brakes grip the rails.
tricks.body_zh: 調速機盯著速度；往下太快，煞車就夾住導軌。

safety.en: Never use an elevator in a fire. After an earthquake, take the stairs too, because the power may fail.
safety.zh: 火災時不可以搭電梯。地震之後也請走樓梯，因為可能會停電。

safety.en: If an earthquake starts while you are in an elevator, crouch down, press the buttons for every floor, and get out at the first floor where it stops.
safety.zh: 在電梯裡遇到地震：蹲低身體，按下所有樓層的按鈕，在第一個停下來的樓層走出去。

safety.en: If the elevator gets stuck, stay calm, press the emergency call button, and wait for help. Do not try to force the doors open.
safety.zh: 電梯卡住時保持冷靜，按緊急呼叫鈕，等人來幫忙。不要自己去扳電梯門。

safety.en: Never put a hand, foot, or bag between closing doors, and keep clothes and bag straps away from them.
safety.zh: 不要把手、腳或包包伸進正在關的門，衣服和背帶也要離門遠一點。

safety.en: Do the activities with an adult. Keep the hanging bottles low over the floor, and do not play with the elevator buttons.
safety.zh: 活動要有大人陪同。吊起來的瓶子離地面低一點；不要玩電梯的按鈕。

activities.title_en: Lift a Bottle with One Finger

materials.en: Two plastic bottles of the same size with caps, and water
materials.zh: 兩個一樣大、有蓋子的寶特瓶，和水

materials.en: A strong string about 1.5 meters long
materials.zh: 一條大約 1.5 公尺的結實繩子

materials.en: A smooth broom handle laid across two chairs (this is your “wheel”)
materials.zh: 一支光滑的掃把柄，橫放在兩張椅子上（當作「輪子」）

steps.en: Fill one bottle with water. This is the car. Tie it to one end of the string and pass the string over the broom handle.
steps.zh: 把一個瓶子裝滿水，這是「車廂」。綁在繩子的一頭，把繩子繞過掃把柄。

steps.en: Pull the other end of the string down with one finger to lift the bottle. How hard is it?
steps.zh: 用一根手指把繩子的另一頭往下拉，把瓶子吊起來。費不費力？

steps.en: Now fill the second bottle almost full and tie it to the other end. This is the counterweight.
steps.zh: 現在把第二個瓶子裝到快滿，綁在繩子的另一頭，這是「平衡錘」。

steps.en: Lift the first bottle again with one finger. What changed? What happens if the counterweight is heavier than the car?
steps.zh: 再用一根手指把第一個瓶子抬起來。有什麼不一樣？如果平衡錘比車廂重，會怎麼樣？

activities.tip_en: The closer the two bottles are in weight, the easier the lift. That is exactly what an elevator's counterweight is for.
activities.tip_zh: 兩個瓶子的重量越接近，就越省力。電梯的平衡錘就是做這件事。

materials.en: An elevator in your school or building, and an adult to ride with you
materials.zh: 學校或大樓裡的一部電梯，和一位陪你搭的大人

materials.en: A notebook and a pencil
materials.zh: 筆記本和鉛筆

steps.en: Inside the car, find the sign that shows the load in kilograms and the number of people allowed. Write both down.
steps.zh: 在車廂裡找出標示載重（公斤）和限乘人數的牌子，把兩個數字抄下來。

steps.en: Divide the kilograms by the number of people. How many kilograms does the sign allow for each person?
steps.zh: 把公斤數除以人數。這塊牌子給每個人算幾公斤？

steps.en: Find the emergency call button. Look at it, but do not press it.
steps.zh: 找出緊急呼叫鈕。看就好，不要按。

steps.en: Ride up one floor. Do you feel a little heavier when the car starts, and a little lighter when it stops?
steps.zh: 往上搭一層樓。車廂啟動時有沒有覺得變重一點、停下來時變輕一點？

activities.tip_en: Ride at a quiet time so you do not keep other people waiting.
activities.tip_zh: 挑人少的時候去，不要讓別人等。

sources.en: Cables over a drive wheel with a counterweight; the counterweight weighs as much as the car plus 40–50% of its capacity
sources.zh: 鋼索繞過曳引輪、另一頭掛平衡錘；平衡錘重量等於車廂加上 40–50% 的載重

sources.en: A car hangs on 2 to 6 (or more) cables, each able to hold the rated load plus 25%; a governor detects overspeed and brake shoes clamp the rails
sources.zh: 車廂掛在 2 到 6 條（或更多）鋼索上，每條都能承受額定載重再加 25%；調速機偵測超速，煞車夾住導軌

sources.en: Elisha Otis: safety device invented in 1853, shown at the New York Crystal Palace in 1854; first passenger safety elevator on March 23, 1857
sources.zh: 奧的斯：1853 年發明安全裝置，1854 年在紐約水晶宮博覽會示範；1857 年 3 月 23 日第一部載客安全電梯啟用

sources.en: At the 1854 demonstration Otis stood on the platform and had the rope cut; the safety device stopped it
sources.zh: 1854 年的示範：奧的斯站在平台上請人砍斷繩子，安全裝置把平台停住

sources.en: Taipei 101 elevators: 5th to 89th floor in 37 seconds at 60.6 km/h (1,010 m/min), the fastest in the world when completed
sources.zh: 台北 101 電梯：5 樓到 89 樓 37 秒，時速 60.6 公里（每分鐘 1,010 公尺），完工時世界最快

sources.en: Taiwan's official term and definition of the counterweight (平衡錘): weights that balance the car and part of the design load
sources.zh: 台灣法規的名稱與定義——平衡錘：平衡昇降機廂靜載重及部分設計載重之一個或數個重物
sources.src: 建築技術規則建築設備編（全國法規資料庫）

sources.en: In an elevator during an earthquake: crouch, press every floor button, get out where it stops; if stuck, use the emergency call button
sources.zh: 地震時在電梯內：蹲低、按下所有樓層按鈕、在停下的樓層走出；卡住時用緊急呼叫鈕求救
sources.src: 臺北市政府消防局防災教育雲

sources.en: Do not use elevators when escaping a fire
sources.zh: 火災逃生避難時不可搭乘電梯

lessons.title: How Does a Refrigerator Keep Food Cold?
lessons.blurb_en: A refrigerator does not make cold. It carries heat out of the food and into your kitchen. Follow the refrigerant around a see-through 3D fridge, then open the door or pull the plug and watch the inside warm up.
lessons.blurb_zh: 冰箱並不是「製造冷」，而是把食物裡的熱搬到廚房去。在透明的 3D 冰箱裡跟著冷媒繞一圈，再把門打開、或把插頭拔掉，看裡面怎麼變暖。
lessons.big_idea_en: A refrigerator does not make cold; it moves heat. A liquid called refrigerant evaporates in tubes inside the refrigerator and soaks up heat from the food. A compressor then squeezes it until it is hot, and a coil on the outside gives that heat to the kitchen. Then the refrigerant goes back inside and does it all again.
lessons.big_idea_zh: 冰箱不是製造冷，而是搬運熱。一種叫冷媒的液體在冰箱裡面的管子蒸發，把食物的熱吸走；壓縮機再把它壓縮到變熱，由外面的散熱管把熱交給廚房。然後冷媒回到裡面，再來一次。

lab.how_en: Drag to turn the view, and scroll or pinch to zoom. You are looking at a see-through refrigerator from behind. Follow the dots from 1 to 4: red means hot, blue means cold. Orange glows are heat, leaving the food and leaving the coil on the back. Press “Open the door,” switch off “Plugged in,” or make the kitchen hotter, and watch the temperature inside.
lab.how_zh: 拖曳可以旋轉視角，滾輪或雙指可以縮放。你是從後面看一台透明的冰箱。跟著小圓點從 1 走到 4：紅色是熱、藍色是冷。橘色的光點是熱，從食物離開、也從背後的散熱管離開。按「把門打開」、關掉「插著電」、或把廚房調熱，看冰箱裡的溫度怎麼變。

legend.en: Red dots: hot refrigerant, squeezed by the compressor
legend.zh: 紅點：被壓縮機壓過、很熱的冷媒

legend.en: Blue dots: cold refrigerant, after the thin tube
legend.zh: 藍點：通過細管之後、很冷的冷媒

legend.en: Big and far apart = gas; small and close together = liquid
legend.zh: 大而稀疏＝氣體；小而密＝液體

legend.en: Orange glows: heat on the move
legend.zh: 橘色光點：正在移動的熱

lab.scale_en: A teaching model. The temperatures come from a simple calculation, not from a real refrigerator, and one second here stands for about four minutes. The bars use example numbers (2 parts of heat moved for 1 part of electricity); real refrigerators differ. The tubes are drawn thicker and far fewer than real ones, real refrigerant stays sealed inside the tubes where you cannot see it, and many refrigerators hide the outside coil in their walls.
lab.scale_zh: 這是教學用的模型。溫度是用簡單的算式算出來的，不是真冰箱量到的；這裡的 1 秒大約代表 4 分鐘。橫槓用的是舉例的數字（用 1 份電搬 2 份熱），真正的冰箱各有不同。管子畫得比真的粗、也少很多；真的冷媒封在管子裡看不到；很多冰箱把外面的散熱管藏在外殼裡。
lab.credit_html: Model drawn by My Culture Connect as a teaching diagram. The four steps of the cycle follow Wikipedia, “Vapor-compression refrigeration”. · 模型由人師教育協會自繪示意；循環的四個步驟依維基百科「Vapor-compression refrigeration」條目。

paras: Open the refrigerator on a hot day and cool air touches your face. Now put your hand on the side of the refrigerator, or near the back. On many refrigerators it feels warm! Why would a machine that keeps food cold be warm on the outside? The answer tells you how a refrigerator really works.

A refrigerator cannot make cold, because cold is not a thing. Cold just means less heat. So a refrigerator does only one job: it takes heat out of the box and puts it somewhere else. To do that, it uses a trick you already know. When you climb out of a swimming pool, the water on your skin dries and you feel chilly. A liquid that evaporates takes heat away with it.

Inside the walls of a refrigerator there is a long tube with a special liquid in it, called refrigerant. In the part of the tube that is inside the box, the refrigerant is very cold, colder than the food. It evaporates and turns into a gas. As it does, it soaks up heat from the air and the food, just like the water drying on your skin.

Next the gas goes to the compressor, the part that hums at the bottom of the refrigerator. The compressor squeezes the gas hard, and squeezing makes it hot, hotter than your kitchen. The hot gas flows through a coil on the outside. There it gives its heat to the room and turns back into a liquid. Then it is pushed through a very thin tube. Its pressure drops suddenly, it becomes very cold, and it goes back inside to start again.

People have used this idea for a long time. In 1834 Jacob Perkins built the first working machine that cooled things this way. Before home refrigerators, families kept food cold with big blocks of ice. The first electric refrigerators for homes were made in 1913. Today the refrigerant in most new refrigerators is a gas called isobutane.

Here is a puzzle. On a hot day, can you cool the kitchen by leaving the refrigerator door open? No! The heat taken from inside comes right back out of the coil into the same room, together with the heat from the electricity. The kitchen gets warmer. So close the door quickly, do not pack the refrigerator too full, and leave some space around it so the heat can get away.
paras_zh: 大熱天打開冰箱，涼涼的空氣撲到臉上。現在把手放在冰箱的側面，或靠近背後的地方——很多冰箱摸起來是溫溫的！一台讓食物保持冰涼的機器，外面為什麼是熱的？答案正好說明了冰箱真正的原理。
冰箱沒辦法「製造冷」，因為冷並不是一種東西，冷只是熱比較少。所以冰箱只做一件事：把箱子裡的熱拿出來，放到別的地方。它用的是你早就知道的一招。從游泳池爬上來時，皮膚上的水慢慢乾掉，你會覺得涼涼的。液體蒸發的時候，會把熱一起帶走。
冰箱的外殼裡有一條長長的管子，裡面裝著一種特別的液體，叫做冷媒。在冰箱裡面的那一段管子，冷媒非常冷，比食物還冷。它蒸發變成氣體，同時把空氣和食物的熱吸走，就像皮膚上乾掉的水一樣。
接著氣體來到壓縮機，也就是冰箱底下嗡嗡響的那個零件。壓縮機用力擠壓氣體，一擠就變熱，比你家的廚房還熱。熱熱的氣體流過外面的散熱管，把熱交給房間，自己變回液體。然後它被推進一條非常細的管子，壓力突然下降，變得非常冷，再回到裡面重新開始。
人們用這個方法已經很久了。1834 年，柏金斯（Jacob Perkins）做出第一台用這種方式冷卻、真的能運轉的機器。家裡有冰箱之前，大家是用大冰塊來保存食物。第一批家用的電冰箱在 1913 年做出來。今天大部分新冰箱用的冷媒，是一種叫異丁烷的氣體。
來猜個謎：大熱天把冰箱門一直開著，廚房會變涼嗎？不會！從裡面搬走的熱，馬上又從散熱管回到同一個房間，還要加上電變成的熱，廚房反而更熱。所以開了門要快點關上，冰箱不要塞太滿，四周也要留一點空間，讓熱散得出去。
questions: What is the one job that a refrigerator really does?
What happens to the refrigerant inside the refrigerator, and what happens to it in the coil outside?
Why does the kitchen get warmer if you leave the refrigerator door open?
answers: It moves heat: it takes heat out of the box and puts it into the room outside.
Inside, the cold refrigerant evaporates into a gas and soaks up heat. In the coil outside, the hot gas gives its heat to the room and turns back into a liquid.
Because the heat taken from inside goes right back into the same room, together with the heat from the electricity the refrigerator uses.

vocab.ex: Put the milk back in the refrigerator.
vocab.exzh: 把牛奶放回冰箱。

vocab.ex: The refrigerant flows through tubes in the walls.
vocab.exzh: 冷媒在外殼裡的管子流動。

vocab.ex: The water on the road evaporated in the sun.
vocab.exzh: 路上的水在太陽下蒸發了。

vocab.ex: You can hear the compressor hum at night.
vocab.exzh: 晚上聽得到壓縮機嗡嗡的聲音。

vocab.ex: Squeeze the bottle to get the last drop out.
vocab.exzh: 擠一擠瓶子，把最後一滴擠出來。

vocab.ex: A towel soaks up water.
vocab.exzh: 毛巾會吸水。

vocab.ex: The temperature inside is four degrees.
vocab.exzh: 裡面的溫度是四度。

vocab.ex: Fish spoils quickly on a hot day.
vocab.exzh: 天氣熱的時候，魚很快就壞掉。

quiz.q: What does a refrigerator really do?
options: It moves heat from inside to outside
It makes cold and adds it to the food
It blows cold air in from outdoors

quiz.q: What happens when the refrigerant evaporates inside the refrigerator?
What does the compressor do to the refrigerant gas?
options: It squeezes the gas and makes it hot
It lets the gas out into the kitchen
It turns the gas into water

quiz.q: Why is the outside of a refrigerator warm?
options: The coil is giving heat to the room
The food inside is too hot
The light inside is always on

quiz.q: You leave the refrigerator door open all afternoon. What happens to the kitchen?

parts_head.eyebrow: Try It in the Model · 在模型裡試試
parts_head.en: Four days in the life of a refrigerator

parts.text_en: The compressor runs until the inside is cold enough, then rests. A little heat leaks in, and it starts again. That is why a refrigerator hums, goes quiet, and hums again.
parts.text_zh: 壓縮機運轉到裡面夠冷，就休息。一點點熱滲進來，它又啟動。所以冰箱會嗡嗡響一陣、安靜一陣、再響一陣。

parts.text_en: Warm air pours in faster than the refrigerant can carry heat away. The inside warms up even though the compressor never stops.
parts.text_zh: 暖空氣湧進來的速度，比冷媒搬熱還快。壓縮機一刻都沒停，裡面還是越來越暖。

parts.text_en: The dots stop. Nothing is moving heat out, so the inside slowly climbs to the temperature of the kitchen. A closed door slows this down.
parts.text_zh: 小圓點停了。沒有東西把熱搬出去，裡面慢慢升到和廚房一樣的溫度。門關著可以拖慢這件事。

parts.text_en: More heat leaks in from a hotter room, so the compressor has to run longer and rest less. That uses more electricity.
parts.text_zh: 房間越熱，滲進來的熱越多，壓縮機就得運轉更久、休息更少，也就更耗電。

lessons.parts_note_en: Watch the three bars: the heat sent to the kitchen is always the heat taken from inside plus the electricity used. That is why an open refrigerator can never cool a room.
lessons.parts_note_zh: 注意三條橫槓：送到廚房的熱，永遠等於從裡面搬走的熱加上用掉的電。所以開著門的冰箱不可能讓房間變涼。

facts.eyebrow: Refrigerators by the Numbers · 冰箱的數字
facts.lead_en: Two dates from history, and four numbers for your own kitchen.
facts.lead_zh: 兩個歷史上的年份，和四個你家廚房用得到的數字。

items.en: Jacob Perkins built the first working refrigeration system that squeezes a gas and lets a liquid evaporate.
items.zh: 柏金斯做出第一台「壓縮氣體、讓液體蒸發」而且真的能運轉的冷凍系統。

items.en: The first electric refrigerators for home use were invented and produced.
items.zh: 第一批家用的電冰箱被發明並生產出來。

items.en: Taiwan's Food and Drug Administration suggests keeping the refrigerator between 0°C and 7°C.
items.zh: 食藥署建議家用冰箱的冷藏溫度維持在 0°C 到 7°C 之間。

items.en: The freezer should stay below −18°C.
items.zh: 冷凍則應該低於 −18°C。

items.en: Germs grow easily between 7°C and 60°C, so food should not sit at room temperature for long.
items.zh: 7°C 到 60°C 之間微生物容易孳生，所以食物不要在室溫放太久。

items.en: Refrigerators in Taiwan carry an energy label from grade 1 to grade 5. Grade 1 uses the least electricity.
items.zh: 台灣的電冰箱有 1 到 5 級的能源效率標示，1 級用電最少。

myths.myth_en: A refrigerator makes cold and puts it into the food.
myths.myth_zh: 冰箱製造「冷」，再把冷放進食物裡。
myths.fact_en: There is no such thing as cold to add. A refrigerator takes heat out of the food and moves it to the room.
myths.fact_zh: 沒有「冷」這種東西可以加進去。冰箱是把食物裡的熱拿出來，搬到房間裡。

myths.myth_en: Leaving the refrigerator door open will cool the kitchen.
myths.myth_zh: 把冰箱門開著，廚房會變涼。
myths.fact_en: The heat comes right back out of the coil into the same room, plus the heat from the electricity. The kitchen gets warmer.
myths.fact_zh: 熱馬上又從散熱管回到同一個房間，還加上電變成的熱，廚房反而更熱。

myths.myth_en: If the outside of the refrigerator feels warm, it is broken.
myths.myth_zh: 冰箱外面摸起來溫溫的，就是壞了。
myths.fact_en: That warmth is the heat that was carried out of the food. Leave space around the refrigerator so it can get away.
myths.fact_zh: 那些溫溫的，正是從食物裡搬出來的熱。冰箱四周要留空間，讓熱散得出去。

myths.myth_en: Food in the refrigerator never goes bad, because the cold kills germs.
myths.myth_zh: 食物放進冰箱就不會壞，因為低溫會殺死細菌。
myths.fact_en: Cold only slows germs down; it does not kill them. Food in the refrigerator still spoils, just more slowly.
myths.fact_zh: 低溫只能讓微生物長得慢，不能殺菌。放在冰箱的食物還是會壞，只是慢一點。

tricks.body_en: A refrigerator does not make cold. It carries heat out.
tricks.body_zh: 冰箱不製造冷，是把熱搬出去。

tricks.body_en: Evaporating soaks up heat inside. Squeezing makes the gas hot enough to give that heat away outside.
tricks.body_zh: 在裡面蒸發吸熱；在外面壓縮變熱，才能把熱送出去。

tricks.title_en: Warm outside means it is working
tricks.title_zh: 外面溫溫的，表示它在工作
tricks.body_en: The heat you feel on the outside came from the food inside.
tricks.body_zh: 你在外面摸到的熱，是從裡面的食物搬出來的。

tricks.body_en: More heat always comes out than was taken in. An open door cannot cool a room.
tricks.body_zh: 送出去的熱永遠比搬走的多，所以開著門不可能讓房間變涼。

safety.en: Never climb into or hide inside a refrigerator or freezer, not even an old one that is unplugged. You could be trapped with no air.
safety.zh: 絕對不可以爬進或躲進冰箱、冰櫃，就算是沒插電的舊冰箱也一樣，可能被關在裡面沒有空氣。

safety.en: Do not touch, pull, or poke the tubes and the compressor at the back. The refrigerant is sealed inside and must stay there.
safety.zh: 不要去摸、拉或戳背後的管子和壓縮機。冷媒封在裡面，不能讓它跑出來。

safety.en: An old refrigerator must go to recycling, where the refrigerant is taken out safely first. Never dump one or take it apart.
safety.zh: 舊冰箱要交給回收，處理時會先把冷媒安全地抽出來。不可以亂丟，也不要自己拆。

safety.en: Do not leave food at room temperature for long. Put leftovers in the refrigerator soon, and keep raw food and cooked food apart.
safety.zh: 食物不要在室溫放太久。吃剩的要盡快冰起來，生的和熟的要分開放。

safety.en: Do the activities with an adult. Do not move the refrigerator by yourself, and close the door quickly after you look inside.
safety.zh: 活動要有大人陪同。不要自己搬動冰箱；看完裡面就趕快把門關上。

materials.en: A cup of water at room temperature
materials.zh: 一杯室溫的水

materials.en: A fan, or a piece of cardboard to wave
materials.zh: 一台電風扇，或一張可以搧風的厚紙板

steps.en: Wet the back of one hand with the water. Keep the other hand dry.
steps.zh: 用水把一隻手的手背弄濕，另一隻手保持乾的。

steps.en: Hold both hands in front of the fan, or have a friend wave the cardboard at them.
steps.zh: 兩隻手一起放在電風扇前面，或請同學用厚紙板對著手搧風。

steps.en: Which hand feels cooler? Keep going until the wet hand is dry. Does the cool feeling stop?
steps.zh: 哪一隻手比較涼？繼續吹到濕的手乾掉，涼涼的感覺還在嗎？

steps.en: The water was not cold. Where did the heat from your skin go?
steps.zh: 水並不冰，那你皮膚上的熱跑到哪裡去了？

activities.tip_en: The water took heat from your skin as it evaporated. Refrigerant does the same thing inside a refrigerator, only much faster.
activities.tip_zh: 水蒸發時把你皮膚的熱帶走了。冷媒在冰箱裡做的是同一件事，只是快得多。

materials.en: The refrigerator at home, and an adult to help
materials.zh: 家裡的冰箱，和一位幫忙的大人

materials.en: A watch or a phone timer, a notebook, and a pencil
materials.zh: 手錶或手機計時器、筆記本和鉛筆

steps.en: Put your hand flat on each side of the refrigerator and on the top. Where does it feel warm?
steps.zh: 把手平貼在冰箱的兩側和上面。哪裡摸起來溫溫的？

steps.en: Find the energy label. Which grade is it, from 1 to 5?
steps.zh: 找出能源效率標示。它是 1 到 5 級裡的第幾級？

steps.en: Listen. Time how long the refrigerator hums and how long it stays quiet. Write both times down.
steps.zh: 仔細聽。計時冰箱嗡嗡響多久、安靜多久，把兩個時間記下來。

steps.en: Try again on a hotter day, or after someone has opened the door many times. Does it hum for longer?
steps.zh: 天氣更熱的時候、或有人開了很多次門之後再量一次。它響得比較久嗎？

activities.tip_en: Some new refrigerators are very quiet, and some change speed instead of stopping. If you cannot hear yours, look for the warm spot instead.
activities.tip_zh: 有些新冰箱很安靜，有些是改變轉速而不是停下來。聽不到的話，就改找摸起來溫溫的地方。

sources.en: The cycle: compressor, condenser, expansion device, evaporator; the refrigerant evaporates to absorb heat and condenses to release it
sources.zh: 循環的四個部分：壓縮機、冷凝器、膨脹裝置、蒸發器；冷媒蒸發吸熱、冷凝放熱

sources.en: Jacob Perkins built the first working vapor-compression system in 1834; first electric home refrigerators in 1913; R-600a (isobutane) is the main refrigerant now used
sources.zh: 柏金斯 1834 年做出第一台能運轉的蒸氣壓縮式系統；1913 年第一批家用電冰箱；現在主要使用的冷媒是 R-600a（異丁烷）

sources.en: A liquid that evaporates takes heat away (evaporative cooling)
sources.zh: 液體蒸發時會帶走熱（蒸發冷卻）

sources.en: Leaving a refrigerator door open makes the room warmer, not cooler
sources.zh: 冰箱門開著，房間只會更熱、不會變涼
sources.src: University of Illinois Physics, “Ask the Van: Open Refrigerator”

sources.en: Home refrigerator 0–7°C, freezer below −18°C; do not overfill; 7–60°C is the danger zone; cold slows germs but does not kill them
sources.zh: 家用冰箱冷藏 0–7°C、冷凍低於 −18°C；不要塞太滿；7–60°C 是危險溫度帶；冰箱是抑制微生物生長而不是殺菌
sources.src: 衛生福利部食品藥物管理署《藥物食品安全週報》

sources.en: Refrigerator energy grades 1 to 5 (grade 1 uses less electricity); leave space around the refrigerator; open the door as little as possible
sources.zh: 電冰箱能源效率分 1 至 5 級（1 級用電較少）；冰箱四周保持空間；盡量減少開門次數

sources.en: Old refrigerators: the refrigerant is removed first when they are recycled
sources.zh: 廢電冰箱回收處理時，拆解前先抽出冷媒
sources.src: 新北市政府環境保護局（資料來源：環境部資源循環署）

sources.en: Children have been trapped inside old refrigerators
sources.zh: 曾有兒童被困在舊冰箱裡

units.blurb_en: The chemistry happening in your sink, your kitchen, and your microwave.
units.blurb_zh: 洗手台、廚房和微波爐裡正在發生的化學。

planned.en: How Does a Microwave Oven Heat Food?
